_meta.scope: Generic OBD-II DTCs only; no manufacturer-specific interpretation.

common_causes: Clock spring (spiral cable) damaged in steering column
Loose or corroded airbag connector under steering wheel
B0001.description: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) module has detected a fault in the deployment control circuit for the first stage of the driver frontal airbag. The SRS warning lamp illuminates and airbag deployment may be impaired in a crash event.
B0001.title: Driver Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control

common_causes: Stage 2 squib circuit open or shorted
B0002.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the deployment control circuit for the second stage of the driver frontal airbag. Dual-stage airbags use two charges for severity-dependent deployment — this code indicates the high-severity stage cannot be triggered reliably.
B0002.title: Driver Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control

common_causes: Shorted squib leads in clock spring or wiring
Internal short within driver airbag module
B0003.description: The SRS module has detected that the resistance in the driver frontal airbag deployment loop is below the expected range, suggesting a short or partial short between the squib leads. The airbag warning lamp is illuminated.
B0003.title: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Resistance Low

B0004.description: The SRS module measured a higher than expected resistance in the driver frontal airbag deployment circuit. Causes include a partially open connection, corroded contacts, or a damaged clock spring conductor.
B0004.title: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Resistance High

common_causes: Wiring harness break in steering column
B0005.description: The SRS module detects an open circuit in the driver frontal airbag deployment loop. The airbag will not deploy in a crash and the SRS warning lamp is illuminated.
B0005.title: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Open

common_causes: Internal airbag module short to housing
B0006.description: One of the deployment leads for the driver frontal airbag is shorted to ground. The SRS module disables deployment of the affected stage to prevent unintended firing.
B0006.title: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Ground

B0007.description: The driver frontal airbag deployment loop is shorted to battery voltage. This is potentially dangerous as it could cause unintended deployment; the SRS module isolates the circuit and sets the warning lamp.
B0007.title: Driver Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Battery

common_causes: Loose or corroded passenger airbag connector
B0010.description: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0010.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Control

common_causes: Stage 2 squib circuit open or shorted
B0011.description: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0011.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control

B0012.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the second-stage deployment circuit of the front passenger airbag. The dual-stage charge cannot be triggered as designed and the airbag warning lamp is illuminated.
B0012.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control

B0013.description: Fault on the deployment control circuit of the passenger knee airbag (knee bolster). Restricts lower-body motion of the passenger in a frontal collision.
B0013.title: Passenger Knee Bolster Deployment Control

B0014.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the driver knee airbag deployment control circuit. The knee airbag may not deploy in a crash event.
B0014.title: Driver Knee Airbag Deployment Control

B0015.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the passenger knee airbag deployment control circuit. Same fault profile as B0014 but for the passenger side.
B0015.title: Passenger Knee Airbag Deployment Control

common_causes: Water at connector causing low resistance
B0016.description: The SRS module detected a short to ground in the front passenger airbag deployment circuit. Deployment of the affected stage is inhibited and the warning lamp is illuminated.
B0016.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Ground

B0017.description: The front passenger airbag deployment loop is shorted to battery voltage, creating a risk of unintended deployment. The SRS module disables the circuit and stores this fault.
B0017.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Loop Short to Battery

B0018.description: The SRS module measures a higher than expected resistance in the passenger frontal deployment loop, indicating partial corrosion or damage. The airbag may not deploy reliably.
B0018.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Loop Resistance High

B0019.description: The SRS module detects too low a resistance in the front passenger airbag deployment loop, suggesting a partial short. Deployment of that stage is inhibited.
B0019.title: Right Front/Passenger Frontal Deployment Loop Resistance Low

B001A.description: Fault on the deployment circuit of the center frontal airbag, deployment stage 3 (highest severity). Used in dual or triple-stage front airbag systems for severe crash energy.
B001A.title: Center Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control

common_causes: Seat harness connector under driver seat damaged
B0020.description: Left Side Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0020.title: Left Side Deployment Control

common_causes: Loose airbag connector under driver seat
B0021.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the deployment control circuit for the left side (driver) airbag stage 1. Side impact protection on the driver side may be reduced.
B0021.title: Left Side Deployment Stage 1 Control

B0022.description: An open circuit has been detected in the deployment loop for the left side airbag stage 1. The airbag will not fire and the SRS lamp is illuminated.
B0022.title: Left Side Deployment Stage 1 Loop Open

common_causes: Chafed wire grounding under seat rail
B0023.description: The left side airbag stage 1 deployment loop is shorted to ground. Deployment is inhibited and the SRS warning lamp is on.
B0023.title: Left Side Deployment Stage 1 Loop Short to Ground

common_causes: Seat harness connector under passenger seat damaged
B0024.description: Right Side Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0024.title: Right Side Deployment Control

B0025.description: A fault is detected in the deployment control for the second stage of the left side airbag, used in vehicles with two-stage side restraint systems.
B0025.title: Left Side Deployment Stage 2 Control

B0026.description: An open circuit is present in the second-stage deployment loop of the left side airbag.
B0026.title: Left Side Deployment Stage 2 Loop Open

common_causes: Curtain airbag squib circuit open or shorted
B0028.description: Driver Side Curtain Air Bag Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0028.title: Driver Side Curtain Air Bag Deployment Control

common_causes: Curtain airbag squib circuit open or shorted
B0029.description: Right Side Curtain Air Bag Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0029.title: Right Side Curtain Air Bag Deployment Control

B002A.description: Fault on the second deployment circuit of the right side curtain airbag. Curtain airbags deploy along the side glass to protect head and neck in a side or rollover crash.
B002A.title: Right Curtain Deployment Control 2

common_causes: Stage 2 squib circuit open or shorted
B0030.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the driver-side curtain airbag stage 2 deployment circuit. Two-stage curtain airbags use a second charge for severe lateral impacts.
B0030.title: Driver Side Curtain Airbag Stage 2

common_causes: Stage 2 squib circuit open or shorted
B0031.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the passenger-side curtain airbag stage 2 deployment circuit. Same fault profile as B0030 but for the passenger side.
B0031.title: Passenger Side Curtain Airbag Stage 2

common_causes: Wire break in passenger seat harness
B0032.description: An open circuit is detected in the right side (passenger) airbag stage 1 deployment loop.
B0032.title: Right Side Deployment Stage 1 Loop Open

B0033.description: The deployment loop for the right side airbag stage 1 is shorted to ground; deployment is inhibited.
B0033.title: Right Side Deployment Stage 1 Loop Short to Ground

B0034.description: The SRS module reports a fault in the deployment circuit of the right side airbag stage 2.
B0034.title: Right Side Deployment Stage 2 Control

B0036.description: The right side airbag stage 2 deployment loop is shorted to ground; the SRS module disables that stage.
B0036.title: Right Side Deployment Stage 2 Loop Short to Ground

B0038.description: Fault on the deployment circuit of the second-row right-side airbag (built into the seat or door for rear-passenger side-impact protection).
B0038.title: Second Row Right Side Airbag Deployment Control

B0039.description: Fault on the second-row right frontal airbag, stage 1 deployment (low severity). Found on vehicles with rear-passenger frontal airbags integrated in the front seatbacks.
B0039.title: Second Row Right Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control

B003A.description: Fault on second-row right frontal airbag, stage 2 deployment (medium severity).
B003A.title: Second Row Right Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control

B003B.description: Fault on second-row right frontal airbag, stage 3 deployment (high severity).
B003B.title: Second Row Right Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control

common_causes: Wiring or connector fault to sensor
B0040.description: The HVAC or body control module has detected an implausible signal from the outside (ambient) temperature sensor. The displayed outside temperature may be wrong or missing and automatic climate control may behave incorrectly.
B0040.title: Outside Temperature Sensor Circuit

B0041.description: Fault on the third-row left frontal airbag, stage 1 deployment.
B0041.title: Third Row Left Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control

B0042.description: A generic open-circuit fault has been reported in a side airbag deployment loop. Refer to vehicle service data to determine the affected side and stage.
B0042.title: Side Deployment Loop Open (Generic)

B0043.description: Fault on third-row left frontal airbag, stage 3 deployment.
B0043.title: Third Row Left Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control

B0046.description: An open circuit has been detected in the deployment loop of the left curtain (head) airbag. Curtain protection on the driver side will not deploy.
B0046.title: Left Curtain Deployment Loop Open

B0047.description: The left curtain airbag deployment loop is shorted to ground; the SRS module inhibits deployment.
B0047.title: Left Curtain Deployment Loop Short to Ground

B0048.description: Fault on third-row right-side airbag deployment circuit.
B0048.title: Third Row Right Side Airbag Deployment Control

B0049.description: Fault on third-row right frontal airbag, stage 1 deployment.
B0049.title: Third Row Right Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control

B004A.description: Fault on third-row right frontal airbag, stage 2 deployment.
B004A.title: Third Row Right Frontal Stage 2 Deployment Control

B004B.description: Fault on third-row right frontal airbag, stage 3 deployment.
B004B.title: Third Row Right Frontal Stage 3 Deployment Control

common_causes: Pretensioner squib circuit open or shorted
B0050.description: Driver Pretensioner Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0050.title: Driver Pretensioner Deployment Control

common_causes: Wiring open between module and squib
B0051.description: The SRS module has detected an open circuit in the driver frontal airbag deployment loop. Resistance is above the upper threshold, indicating broken wiring or a disconnected igniter.
B0051.title: Driver Frontal Deployment Control Open

B0052.description: Fault on the passenger seat belt buckle/tongue sensor that detects whether the belt is fastened.
B0052.title: Passenger Seat Belt Sensor

common_causes: Pretensioner squib circuit open or shorted
B0053.description: Passenger Pretensioner Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0053.title: Passenger Pretensioner Deployment Control

B0054.description: Fault on the second-row center seat belt buckle sensor.
B0054.title: Second Row Center Seat Belt Sensor

B0055.description: Fault on the second-row right seat belt buckle sensor.
B0055.title: Second Row Right Seat Belt Sensor

B0056.description: The right curtain airbag deployment circuit shows an open condition; the curtain on the passenger side cannot deploy.
B0056.title: Right Curtain Deployment Loop Open

B0057.description: The right curtain airbag deployment loop is shorted to ground.
B0057.title: Right Curtain Deployment Loop Short to Ground

B0058.description: Fault on the third-row right seat belt buckle sensor.
B0058.title: Third Row Right Seat Belt Sensor

B0060.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the deployment control circuit of a knee airbag. Knee protection in a frontal collision may be reduced.
B0060.title: Knee Airbag Deployment Control

B0061.description: An open is detected in the knee airbag deployment loop.
B0061.title: Knee Airbag Deployment Loop Open

B0062.description: The knee airbag deployment loop is shorted to ground.
B0062.title: Knee Airbag Deployment Loop Short to Ground

B0064.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the driver seat belt tension sensor. This sensor measures belt load and is used by adaptive restraint systems to scale airbag deployment force based on occupant size.
B0064.title: Driver Seat Belt Tension Sensor

B0070.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the rollover sensor circuit. The rollover sensor triggers curtain airbags and seat belt pretensioners when the vehicle approaches a tip-over angle.
B0070.title: Vehicle Rollover Sensor

B0071.description: Fault on the first-row center seat belt pretensioner deployment circuit. Pretensioners pull belt slack tight at the moment of impact.
B0071.title: First Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control

B0072.description: The SRS module detects an open circuit in the driver seatbelt pretensioner deployment loop. The pretensioner cannot fire and the airbag warning lamp is on.
B0072.title: Driver Seatbelt Pretensioner Loop Open

B0073.description: The driver seatbelt pretensioner deployment circuit is shorted to ground.
B0073.title: Driver Seatbelt Pretensioner Loop Short to Ground

B0074.description: The driver seatbelt pretensioner deployment circuit is shorted to battery voltage, risking unintended firing.
B0074.title: Driver Seatbelt Pretensioner Loop Short to Battery

B0075.description: Fault on the second-row right seat belt pretensioner deployment circuit.
B0075.title: Second Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control

B0076.description: The pretensioner deployment loop resistance is below the expected window, suggesting a partial short.
B0076.title: Driver Seatbelt Pretensioner Resistance Low

B0077.description: The driver seatbelt pretensioner loop resistance is above the expected window. The pretensioner may not fire reliably.
B0077.title: Driver Seatbelt Pretensioner Resistance High

B0078.description: Fault on the third-row right seat belt pretensioner deployment circuit.
B0078.title: Third Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner Deployment Control

B0079.description: Fault on the driver seat belt pretensioner B deployment circuit. Pretensioner B is a secondary tightening stage on systems with multi-stage pretensioners.
B0079.title: Driver Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control

B007A.description: Fault on passenger seat belt pretensioner B deployment circuit.
B007A.title: Passenger Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control

B007B.description: Fault on second-row left seat belt pretensioner B deployment circuit.
B007B.title: Second Row Left Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control

B007C.description: Fault on second-row right seat belt pretensioner B deployment circuit.
B007C.title: Second Row Right Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control

B007D.description: Fault on second-row center seat belt pretensioner B deployment circuit.
B007D.title: Second Row Center Seat Belt Pretensioner B Deployment Control

B007E.description: Fault on driver seat belt pretensioner C deployment circuit. Pretensioner C is a third-stage tightener on systems with three-stage pretensioners.
B007E.title: Driver Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control

B007F.description: Fault on passenger seat belt pretensioner C deployment circuit.
B007F.title: Passenger Seat Belt Pretensioner C Deployment Control

B0080.description: Fault on the driver seat belt load limiter deployment circuit. Load limiters release belt webbing under high force to limit chest loads after the pretensioner has tightened the belt.
B0080.title: Driver Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control

B0081.description: The SRS or body control module has detected a fault in the front passenger seat belt buckle switch circuit. The switch reports whether the belt is fastened and is used for the belt warning lamp and for restraint logic.
B0081.title: Front Passenger Belt Switch Circuit

B0082.description: The passenger seatbelt pretensioner deployment loop is open; the pretensioner will not fire.
B0082.title: Passenger Seatbelt Pretensioner Loop Open

B0083.description: The passenger pretensioner deployment circuit is shorted to ground.
B0083.title: Passenger Seatbelt Pretensioner Loop Short to Ground

B0084.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the driver belt buckle switch circuit. The fastened-state of the seat belt cannot be reliably read — affects belt warning and airbag deployment logic.
B0084.title: Driver Belt Buckle Switch Circuit

B0085.description: The SRS module has detected a fault in the passenger belt buckle switch circuit. Same fault profile as B0084 but for the passenger side.
B0085.title: Passenger Belt Buckle Switch Circuit

B0086.description: The passenger seatbelt pretensioner loop has below-normal resistance, indicating a partial short.
B0086.title: Passenger Seatbelt Pretensioner Resistance Low

B0087.description: The passenger pretensioner loop resistance is too high, suggesting corroded contacts or partial breaks.
B0087.title: Passenger Seatbelt Pretensioner Resistance High

B0088.description: Fault on the third-row right seat belt load limiter deployment circuit.
B0088.title: Third Row Right Seat Belt Load Limiter Deployment Control

common_causes: Stage 2 squib circuit open or shorted
B0091.description: Passenger Side Pretensioner Stage 2 Deployment Control: the restraints module has detected a fault in this airbag/pretensioner deployment circuit, which may prevent correct deployment in a crash. Safety-critical.
B0091.title: Passenger Side Pretensioner Stage 2 Deployment Control

B0092.description: The SRS module reports that the left front side impact sensor is malfunctioning. Side airbag deployment may not occur correctly in a side crash.

B0096.description: The left rear side impact sensor is reporting a fault.

B0097.description: The right rear side impact sensor is reporting a malfunction or implausible signal.

common_causes: Seat harness connector under passenger seat damaged

common_causes: Power supply or ground fault to module

C0230.description: The brake pedal position sensor reports an implausible signal. Required for brake-by-wire and stability control.
C0230.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor Circuit

C0234.description: The ABS control module has detected that one of the wheel speed sensor signals has a frequency outside the plausible range, e.g. unrealistically high pulses or signal dropouts at speed. Stability control may be limited.

C0235.description: The ABS control module has detected an erratic wheel speed sensor signal — sudden jumps or dropouts compared to the other wheels. Typical causes are a damaged tone ring or a loose sensor.
C0235.title: Wheel Speed Sensor Signal Erratic

C0237.description: The ABS control module has lost the wheel speed signal from the front left wheel during driving. ABS and stability control are disabled because wheel-individual speed information is required for slip detection.
C0237.title: Loss of Speed Sensor Signal Front Left

common_causes: Tyre sizes or wear levels do not match across axles
Tone ring missing teeth on one wheel
C0238.description: The ABS control module has detected an implausible speed difference between wheels that cannot be explained by cornering. This typically points to one suspect sensor, mismatched tyre sizes or a damaged tone ring.
C0238.title: Speed Wheel-to-Wheel Mismatch

C0240.description: The ABS or stability control module has detected a fault in a brake pressure sensor. Pressure information is used by ESP and brake assist to determine driver intent and modulation pressure during regulation.

C0241.description: The ABS warning lamp control circuit is shorted or open. The driver may see a permanently lit or non-functional ABS warning lamp.

C0242.description: The powertrain control module reports a fault that the ABS module must consider (e.g. traction control engine torque request fault).

C0244.description: The PWM control of the brake pressure modulation valves is faulty.
C0244.title: PWM Brake Pressure Modulation Circuit

C0245.description: The ABS control module has detected that the frequency of one wheel speed sensor signal does not match the others under stable driving conditions. This often indicates a tone ring with extra or missing teeth or a sensor with degraded signal quality.
C0245.title: Wheel Speed Sensor Frequency Mismatch

C0246.description: Internal plausibility check of the combined ABS/TCS control module fails.

common_causes: Power steering fluid low or contaminated
C0250.description: The power steering control module has detected an implausible pressure or load signal from the steering pump. On hydraulic systems this may indicate low fluid or a worn pump; on electric systems it may indicate excessive motor load.

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
C0252.description: The pump motor ground return is open. The motor cannot run, and the system disables ABS and stability control.

C0258.description: The brake booster vacuum sensor reports an implausible signal; brake assist functions are reduced. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

C0265.description: The Electronic Brake Control Module has detected a fault in its main supply relay circuit. Without proper relay supply the EBCM cannot operate the hydraulic unit and ABS as well as stability control are disabled.

common_causes: Active booster motor or solenoid failed
Vacuum supply weak (vacuum pump or hose fault)
C0266.description: The brake control module has detected a fault in the active (electric or vacuum-controlled) brake booster. Active boosters are used by emergency brake assist and adaptive cruise control to autonomously build brake pressure.

C0267.description: The ABS or brake control module has detected an electrical fault in the brake pump motor circuit. The pump is used to build brake pressure during ABS, ESP and brake-by-wire operations and a fault disables these functions.
C0267.title: Brake Pump Motor Circuit

C0268.description: The brake control module has detected that the brake pump has run longer than the allowed maximum time. This typically indicates the pump cannot reach target pressure due to a hydraulic leak, air in the system or a worn pump.
C0268.title: Brake Pump Run Time Exceeded

C0269.description: The brake control module has detected an implausible signal from the vacuum sensor on the brake booster. Modern systems monitor booster vacuum to ensure brake assist is available, especially with stop-start engines and electric vacuum pumps.
C0269.title: Brake Vacuum Sensor

common_causes: Wiring or connector fault to sensor
C0273.description: The brake control module has detected an out-of-range or implausible signal from the brake booster pressure sensor. Brake assist and electronic boost functions may be limited.
C0273.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction

C0277.description: The brake control module has detected an implausible signal from the booster vacuum sensor. Loss of vacuum signal can cause hard pedal and reduced power assist.
C0277.title: Brake Booster Vacuum Sensor Circuit Malfunction

C0279.description: The brake control module has detected an electrical fault in the booster boost (assist pressure) sensor circuit. Power-assist regulation may default to a backup strategy.
C0279.title: Brake Booster Boost Sensor Circuit Malfunction

C0287.description: The stability control module has detected that overall ESP performance is degraded — typically a plausibility check between yaw rate, lateral acceleration, steering angle and wheel speeds has failed. ESP is deactivated until the root cause is resolved.

C0288.description: The stability control module has detected that the yaw rate sensor signal is outside the plausible range during stable driving. This typically indicates a sensor offset, an incorrect mounting or a degraded sensor element.

C0951.description: The TPMS sensor at the front right wheel does not transmit a valid signal.
C0951.title: Tire Pressure Monitoring Sensor Front Right

C0952.description: The TPMS sensor at the rear left wheel does not transmit a valid signal.
C0952.title: Tire Pressure Monitoring Sensor Rear Left

C0953.description: The TPMS sensor at the rear right wheel does not transmit a valid signal.
C0953.title: Tire Pressure Monitoring Sensor Rear Right

C0960.description: The tire pressure monitoring module fails its internal self-test.
C0960.title: Tire Pressure Monitoring Module Internal Fault

P0001.description: The ECU detects an open circuit in the control of fuel volume regulator A (often the metering valve on the high-pressure fuel pump). The actuator does not respond, so rail pressure cannot be controlled accurately.
P0001.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit/Open

common_causes: High-pressure pump worn or leaking internally
P0002.description: The control signal of fuel volume regulator A is electrically present but the actual rail pressure does not follow the target value within tolerance. Indicates a mechanical or hydraulic issue rather than pure wiring.
P0002.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0003.description: The ECU sees the control voltage of fuel volume regulator A pulled below the expected range, typically a short to ground or a low-resistance fault in the wiring or coil.
P0003.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0004.description: The ECU sees the control voltage of fuel volume regulator A above the expected range, typically a short to power or open ground return.
P0004.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit High

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P0005.description: Open circuit detected at the fuel shutoff valve A solenoid (used on diesels to stop fuel flow at engine-off and as anti-theft). Engine may not start or not stop cleanly.
P0005.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0006.description: Control voltage of fuel shutoff valve A is below the expected range, typically caused by a short to ground or low-resistance fault in the solenoid circuit.
P0006.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0007.description: Control voltage of fuel shutoff valve A is above the expected range, typically caused by a short to power or open ground return.
P0007.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High

P0008.description: The ECU detects an implausible relationship between crankshaft and camshaft signals on bank 1, indicating timing chain stretch, jumped tooth, or sensor reluctor wear.
P0008.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 1

common_causes: Chain jumped one tooth on bank 2
P0009.description: Same fault pattern as P0008 but on bank 2 of a V or boxer engine. Crank/cam correlation outside spec on the second cylinder bank.
P0009.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 2

common_causes: Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity
P000A.description: The intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 responds too slowly to commanded position changes. Often caused by VVT solenoid sticking, oil aging, or low oil pressure.
P000A.title: A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1

P000B.description: The exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 responds too slowly to commanded position changes. Same root causes as P000A but on the exhaust cam.
P000B.title: B Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1

P000C.description: Intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 responds too slowly. Same fault pattern as P000A on the second cylinder bank.
P000C.title: A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 2

P000D.description: Exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 responds too slowly. Same fault pattern as P000B on the second cylinder bank.
P000D.title: B Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 2

P000E.description: The ECU's adaptive correction of fuel volume regulator A has reached its learning limit. Indicates a long-term drift between commanded and actual rail pressure that could no longer be compensated.
P000E.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit

P000F.description: The mechanical pressure relief valve on the fuel rail has opened due to overpressure. Indicates a malfunction of the rail pressure regulation that drove pressure beyond the safe limit.
P000F.title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated

common_causes: Wiring or connector fault to actuator
P0010.description: An electrical fault in the bank 1 intake camshaft position actuator solenoid (variable valve timing). The ECU monitors current and feedback on the oil control valve and sets this code when the circuit is open, shorted, or out of range.
P0010.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)

common_causes: Sludge or debris in VVT oil passages
Low engine oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity
P0011.description: The bank 1 intake camshaft is more advanced than commanded, or the actuator does not respond as expected. Often caused by stuck-open oil control valves, sludge in VVT passages, or low oil pressure.
P0011.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)

P0012.description: The bank 1 intake camshaft remains retarded compared to commanded position. Common causes include a stuck-closed oil control valve, blocked oil passages, or a worn cam phaser.
P0012.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)

P0013.description: Electrical fault in the bank 1 exhaust camshaft position actuator solenoid. Same diagnostic principle as P0010 but on the exhaust cam.
P0013.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)

P0014.description: Exhaust camshaft position bank 1 over-advanced or system performance — the actual cam phase exceeds the commanded value. Usually caused by a stuck-open oil control valve, low oil pressure, sludged passages, or a worn cam phaser. Confirm with a scan tool live data: command 0° advance and watch actual.
P0014.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)

P0015.description: The bank 1 exhaust camshaft remains retarded relative to commanded position. Same root causes as P0012 but on the exhaust cam.
P0015.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)

P0016.description: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P0016.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)

P0017.description: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P0017.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B)

P0018.description: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor A): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P0018.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor A)

P0019.description: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor B): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P0019.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor B)

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P001A.description: Open circuit at the camshaft profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 1). Used by systems with discrete cam-lift levels (e.g. BMW Valvetronic, Honda VTEC, Audi AVS) — the actuator that selects the lift profile cannot be driven.
P001A.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P001B.description: Low control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 1). Typically a short to ground in the wiring or actuator coil.
P001B.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P001C.description: Excessively high control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 1). Typically a short to power or open ground.
P001C.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 1

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P001D.description: Open circuit at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 2). Same fault as P001A but on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P001D.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P001E.description: Low control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 2). Same fault as P001B on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P001E.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P001F.description: Excessively high control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 2). Same fault as P001C on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P001F.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 2

P0020.description: Electrical fault in the bank 2 intake camshaft position actuator. Same diagnostic principle as P0010 but on the second cylinder bank.
P0020.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)

P0021.description: The bank 2 intake camshaft is more advanced than commanded, or the actuator does not respond as expected. Often caused by stuck-open oil control valves, sludge in VVT passages, or low oil pressure.
P0021.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 2)

P0022.description: The bank 2 intake camshaft remains retarded compared to commanded position. Common causes include a stuck-closed oil control valve, blocked oil passages, or a worn cam phaser.
P0022.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)

P0023.description: Electrical fault in the bank 2 exhaust camshaft position actuator. Same diagnostic principle as P0013 but on the second cylinder bank.
P0023.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)

P0024.description: The bank 2 exhaust camshaft is more advanced than commanded. Same root causes as P0011 but on the exhaust cam.
P0024.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 2)

P0025.description: The bank 2 exhaust camshaft remains retarded relative to commanded position. Same root causes as P0012 but on the exhaust cam.
P0025.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)

common_causes: Sludge or debris in oil passages
Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity
P0026.description: The ECU detected that the bank 1 intake valve oil control solenoid does not respond as expected. Common causes are sludge in the oil passages, a sticking solenoid, or low oil pressure that prevents proper VVT phasing on the intake side.
P0026.title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)

common_causes: Oil control valve clogged with sludge
Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity
P0027.description: The ECU detects that the exhaust camshaft oil control valve on bank 1 does not respond to commanded duty cycle within expected limits. Camshaft phase deviates from target during phaser actuation tests.
P0027.title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1

common_causes: Sludge or debris in oil passages
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0028.description: The ECU detected that the bank 2 intake valve oil control solenoid does not respond as expected. Common causes are sludge in the oil passages, a sticking solenoid, or low oil pressure that prevents proper VVT phasing on the intake side.
P0028.title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)

common_causes: Oil control valve clogged with sludge
Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity
P0029.description: The ECU detects that the exhaust camshaft oil control valve on bank 2 does not respond to commanded duty cycle within expected limits. Camshaft phase deviates from target during phaser actuation tests.
P0029.title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P002A.description: Open circuit at the cam profile actuator on the exhaust cam (profile A, bank 1). Same diagnosis as P001A but for the exhaust profile actuator.
P002A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P002B.description: Low control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1). Short to ground in wiring or coil.
P002B.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P002C.description: Excessively high control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1). Short to power or open ground.
P002C.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 1

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P002D.description: Open circuit at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2). Same as P002A on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P002D.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P002E.description: Low control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2). Same as P002B on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P002E.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P002F.description: Excessively high control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2). Same as P002C on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P002F.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 2

common_causes: Heater element open or burnt out
P0030.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0030.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)

common_causes: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0031.description: O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1, sensor 1 reports low voltage. Likely shorted to ground or open in the heater control wire. The heater warms the sensor element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0031.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)

common_causes: Heater wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0032.description: O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1, sensor 1 reports high voltage. Likely shorted to B+ or open in the heater element itself. The heater warms the sensor element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0032.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)

common_causes: Open or shorted wiring to solenoid
P0033.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the turbocharger bypass (wastegate) valve control circuit. Voltage or current measured on the solenoid output deviates from expected values during commanded actuation.
P0033.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0034.description: The bypass valve solenoid control circuit reports a voltage below threshold, indicating a short to ground or open driver. The ECU disables boost control until the fault clears.
P0034.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to battery voltage
Open circuit in wiring or solenoid
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0035.description: The bypass valve solenoid control circuit reports a voltage above threshold, indicating a short to power or open circuit. Boost control is disabled while the fault is active.
P0035.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit High

P0036.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0036.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0037.description: O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1, sensor 2 reports low voltage. Likely shorted to ground or open in the heater control wire. The heater warms the sensor element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0037.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0038.description: The heater control line for the upstream bank 1 oxygen sensor reads above the expected voltage, typical of a short to supply.
P0038.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

P0039.description: The wastegate or bypass valve A on the turbo/supercharger does not respond mechanically as expected to its control signal. Boost pressure deviates from target.
P0039.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Range/Performance

P003A.description: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
P003A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit

P003B.description: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
P003B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Position Exceeded Learning Limit

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P003C.description: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1) does not engage when commanded — stays in low-lift profile. Often hydraulic pin sticking or low oil pressure.
P003C.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P003D.description: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1) stays engaged when commanded off — stuck in high-lift profile. Idle quality and emissions affected.
P003D.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 1

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P003E.description: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2) does not engage when commanded — stays in low-lift profile. Often hydraulic pin sticking or low oil pressure.
P003E.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P003F.description: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2) stays engaged when commanded off — stuck in high-lift profile. Idle quality and emissions affected.
P003F.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 2

P0040.description: The pre-cat oxygen sensors of bank 1 and bank 2 appear to be wired the wrong way around — bank 1 reacts when bank 2 should and vice versa. Typically after recent service.
P0040.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 1

P0041.description: The post-cat oxygen sensors of bank 1 and bank 2 appear to be wired the wrong way around — bank 1 reacts when bank 2 should and vice versa. Typically after recent service.
P0041.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 2/Bank 2 Sensor 2

P0042.description: Generic electrical fault in the heater control of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor (typically a third sensor downstream of multi-stage cat or NOx trap).
P0042.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0043.description: Heater control voltage of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor is below the expected range — short to ground or low-resistance fault.
P0043.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0044.description: Heater control voltage of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor is above the expected range — short to power or open ground.
P0044.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P0045.description: Open circuit at the boost control solenoid/actuator A. The ECU cannot drive the wastegate or VGT vanes.
P0045.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit/Open

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0046.description: Boost control actuator A is electrically active but boost pressure deviates from target. Mechanical or hydraulic limitation.
P0046.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0047.description: Boost control circuit A voltage below expected range — short to ground or low-resistance fault in solenoid wiring.
P0047.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0048.description: Boost control circuit A voltage above expected range — short to power or open ground in solenoid wiring.
P0048.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit High

P0049.description: The turbocharger A turbine speed exceeded its safe limit. Risk of bearing damage and shaft fracture. Often caused by a stuck-closed wastegate or boost control fault.
P0049.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Turbine Overspeed

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P004A.description: Open circuit at boost control solenoid B (twin-turbo or two-stage system). Same diagnosis as P0045 on actuator B.
P004A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit/Open

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P004B.description: Boost control B mechanical/hydraulic deviation from target. Same as P0046 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P004B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P004C.description: Boost control B circuit voltage below expected range. Same as P0047 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P004C.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P004D.description: Boost control B circuit voltage above expected range. Same as P0048 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P004D.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P004E.description: Intermittent dropouts or noise on boost control A circuit. Loose connector, partial wiring break, or solenoid degrading.
P004E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P004F.description: Same intermittent fault pattern as P004E on boost control B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P004F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P0050.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0050.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0051.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0051.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0052.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0052.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)

P0053.description: The heater resistance of the bank 1, sensor 1 oxygen sensor is outside its specified range. Sensor heater aging or short between heater and signal.
P0053.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 1

P0054.description: The heater resistance of the bank 1, sensor 2 oxygen sensor is outside its specified range. Sensor heater aging or short between heater and signal.
P0054.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 2

P0055.description: The heater resistance of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor is outside its specified range. Sensor heater aging or short between heater and signal.
P0055.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 3

P0056.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0056.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0057.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0057.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0058.description: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
P0058.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

P0059.description: Heater resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 1 (pre-cat). Same diagnostic as P0053 on the second bank.
P0059.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 1

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P005A.description: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 1 stuck disengaged. Same fault pattern as P003C but on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P005A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P005B.description: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 1 stuck engaged. Same fault pattern as P003D on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P005B.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 1

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P005C.description: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 2 stuck disengaged. Same fault pattern as P003C but on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P005C.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P005D.description: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 2 stuck engaged. Same fault pattern as P003D on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
P005D.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 2

common_causes: Supply fuse blown or relay failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P005E.description: Supply voltage feeding boost control actuator B is below the expected range. Likely fuse, supply wiring or relay fault.
P005E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Supply Voltage Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P005F.description: Supply voltage feeding boost control actuator B is above the expected range. Likely charging system overvoltage or wiring shorted to a higher potential.
P005F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Supply Voltage Circuit High

P0060.description: Heater resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 2 (post-cat). Same diagnostic as P0053 on second bank, post-cat.
P0060.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 2

P0061.description: Heater resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 3. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0061.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 3

P0062.description: Generic electrical fault in the heater control of bank 2 sensor 3. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0062.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0063.description: Heater control voltage of bank 2 sensor 3 below the expected range. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0063.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 3

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
