P00CA.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P00CB.description: Open circuit on the supply voltage feed to the fuel volume regulator solenoid.
P00CB.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit/Open

common_causes: Supply fuse blown or relay failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P00CC.description: Supply voltage to fuel volume regulator solenoid below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P00CC.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P00CD.description: Supply voltage to fuel volume regulator solenoid above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P00CD.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Solenoid Supply Voltage Control Circuit High

P00CE.description: Multiple intake air temperature sensors on bank 1 disagree beyond plausible limits. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00CE.title: Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1

P00CF.description: Barometric pressure and boost sensor A readings disagree at engine off — they should match without boost.
P00CF.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation

P00D0.description: Barometric pressure and boost sensor B readings disagree at engine off — they should match without boost.
P00D0.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00D1.description: Heater control of bank 1 sensor 1 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
P00D1.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00D2.description: Heater control of bank 1 sensor 2 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
P00D2.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00D3.description: Heater control of bank 2 sensor 1 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
P00D3.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 1

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00D4.description: Heater control of bank 2 sensor 2 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
P00D4.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 2

P00D5.description: Pre- and post-cat oxygen sensors on bank 1 do not correlate as expected — typical sign of catalyst inefficiency or one failed sensor.
P00D5.title: HO2S Sensor Correlation Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 1 Sensor 2

P00D6.description: Pre- and post-cat oxygen sensors on bank 2 do not correlate as expected — typical sign of catalyst inefficiency or one failed sensor.
P00D6.title: HO2S Sensor Correlation Bank 2 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 2

common_causes: Cooling system not adequately removing heat
P00D7.description: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
P00D7.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Temperature Too High

P00D8.description: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
P00D8.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Temperature Too High

P00D9.description: Generic electrical fault on ambient air temperature sensor B (second sensor for redundancy or second measurement location).
P00D9.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00DA.description: Ambient air temperature sensor B reading implausible compared to other sources.
P00DA.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B Range/Performance

P00DB.description: Ambient air temp sensor B signal voltage below expected range.
P00DB.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B Low

P00DC.description: Ambient air temp sensor B signal voltage above expected range.
P00DC.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P00DD.description: Intermittent signal from ambient air temp sensor B.
P00DD.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B Intermittent/Erratic

P00DE.description: Generic electrical fault at the charge air cooler coolant temperature sensor A (water-cooled CAC system).
P00DE.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00DF.description: CAC coolant temp sensor A reading implausible. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
P00DF.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P00E0.description: CAC coolant temp sensor A signal voltage below expected range. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
P00E0.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P00E1.description: CAC coolant temp sensor A signal voltage above expected range. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
P00E1.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P00E2.description: Intermittent signal from CAC coolant temp sensor A. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
P00E2.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P00E3.description: The exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A is stuck open. Engine warms up too slowly because exhaust does not heat the heat exchanger.
P00E3.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Stuck Open

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P00E4.description: The exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A is stuck closed. Risk of overheating because exhaust always passes through the heat exchanger.
P00E4.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed

P00E5.description: Intake air and fuel temperature readings are inconsistent — at long soak both should match ambient. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00E5.title: Intake Air Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation

P00E6.description: Multiple intake air pressure sensors on bank 2 disagree with each other beyond the plausible deviation. One has drifted.
P00E6.title: Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2

P00E7.description: Multiple intake air temperature sensors on bank 2 disagree beyond plausible limits. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00E7.title: Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2

P00E8.description: Generic electrical fault on intake air temperature sensor 3 (third measurement location, e.g. in throttle or after intercooler) on bank 1.
P00E8.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Bank 1

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00E9.description: IAT sensor 3 reading on bank 1 implausible. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00E9.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P00EA.description: IAT sensor 3 bank 1 signal voltage below expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00EA.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Low Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P00EB.description: IAT sensor 3 bank 1 signal voltage above expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00EB.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High Bank 1

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P00EC.description: Intermittent signal from IAT sensor 3 on bank 1. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00EC.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1

P00ED.description: Generic electrical fault on intake air temperature sensor 3 (third measurement location, e.g. in throttle or after intercooler) on bank 2.
P00ED.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Bank 2

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00EE.description: IAT sensor 3 reading on bank 2 implausible. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00EE.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P00EF.description: IAT sensor 3 bank 2 signal voltage below expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00EF.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Low Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P00F0.description: IAT sensor 3 bank 2 signal voltage above expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00F0.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High Bank 2

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P00F1.description: Intermittent signal from IAT sensor 3 on bank 2. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P00F1.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P00F2.description: Open circuit at the humidity sensor (used by ECU for combustion correction, especially on direct-injection engines).
P00F2.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit/Open

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00F3.description: Humidity sensor reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P00F3.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P00F4.description: Humidity sensor signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P00F4.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P00F5.description: Humidity sensor signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P00F5.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P00F6.description: Intermittent signal from humidity sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P00F6.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P00F7.description: The relationship between barometric pressure and turbo inlet pressure (bank 2) is implausible — at engine off the two should match. Indicates an inlet sensor or barometric sensor fault.
P00F7.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 2

P00F8.description: Generic electrical fault on turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A (post-compressor pressure measurement).
P00F8.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P00F9.description: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A reading implausible. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P00F9.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P00FA.description: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P00FA.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P00FB.description: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P00FB.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P00FC.description: Intermittent signal from turbo outlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P00FC.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic

P00FD.description: State of charge of battery B (typically auxiliary or hybrid battery) shows performance fault — does not behave according to charging model.
P00FD.title: Battery B State of Charge Performance

P00FE.description: The EVAP tank vapor line is restricted or blocked. Tank pressure cannot equalize properly. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
P00FE.title: EVAP System Tank Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked

common_causes: Underlying BCM fault — read BCM codes
P00FF.description: The Body Control Module (BCM) sent a request to the engine ECU to illuminate the MIL — actual fault is in a body system; this is a forwarded request, not a powertrain fault.
P00FF.title: Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination

P0100.description: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit. The signal is missing, out of plausible range, or the wiring shows continuity issues. Used as a generic fault when no more specific MAF code applies.
P0100.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Malfunction

P0101.description: The mass air flow (MAF) sensor signal is outside the expected range or does not track engine load plausibly. The ECU compares MAF readings against load calculated from RPM, throttle position and intake pressure; persistent disagreement triggers this code.
P0101.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance

P0102.description: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value below the plausible minimum for current engine speed and load. The ECU substitutes a calculated load value while the fault is active.
P0102.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Low Input

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0103.description: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value above the plausible maximum for current engine speed and load. Often indicates a sensor that is failing in a way that produces excess output, or a short to supply voltage in the signal path.
P0103.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit High Input

P0104.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts or noise on the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit. The fault is not constantly present, suggesting a loose connection, intermittent wiring break, or a failing sensor under specific conditions (vibration, temperature).
P0104.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor cracked or disconnected
P0105.description: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) or barometric pressure sensor circuit. Signal missing, implausible, or wiring broken. Generic fault when no more specific MAP code applies.
P0105.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor cracked or detached
P0106.description: The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor signal is implausible relative to throttle position and engine speed. The ECU expects MAP to rise with throttle opening and fall under deceleration; deviation triggers the code.
P0106.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Range/Performance

P0107.description: The MAP sensor reports a pressure below the lower threshold the ECU expects at any engine state. Typically indicates a hard electrical fault rather than a slow drift.
P0107.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Low Input

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
P0108.description: The MAP sensor reports a pressure above the upper threshold the ECU expects in any engine state. Typically caused by a short in the signal circuit or a sensor that has failed producing a fixed high output.
P0108.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor High Input

P0109.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the MAP/BARO sensor circuit. Fault is not constantly present — typically caused by loose connectors, chafed wiring, or a sensor failing under thermal load.
P0109.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Intermittent

P010A.description: Generic electrical fault on MAF sensor B (second sensor for redundancy or twin-intake systems).
P010A.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P010B.description: MAF sensor B reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P010B.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P010C.description: MAF B signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P010C.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P010D.description: MAF B signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P010D.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P010E.description: Intermittent signal from MAF sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P010E.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P010F.description: MAF sensor A and B disagree beyond plausible deviation. One is reading incorrectly.
P010F.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation

P0110.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault in the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor circuit. Signal absent, shorted or out of plausible range. Generic catch-all when no more specific IAT code (low/high/range) is set.
P0110.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: Sensor element coated with oil or dirt
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0111.description: The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor reading does not change plausibly with engine warm-up or after driving begins. Many vehicles share the IAT into the MAF housing; on those, MAF replacement also replaces IAT.
P0111.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance

P0112.description: The IAT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot intake (low NTC resistance). Usually a wiring short to ground or a failed sensor.
P0112.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Low Input

common_causes: Open circuit in sensor or wiring
P0113.description: The IAT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold intake (open-circuit-like behaviour). Usually open wiring or a sensor that has failed open.
P0113.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0114.description: The IAT signal shows intermittent dropouts or jumps that fall outside slope expectations but do not stay above or below threshold long enough to trigger P0112/P0113. Usually a wiring or connector issue.
P0114.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Intermittent

P0115.description: A general fault has been detected in the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. The ECU uses ECT for fuel enrichment during cold start, fan control, and closed-loop entry timing.
P0115.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: Thermostat stuck open (engine never reaches operating temperature)
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0116.description: The coolant temperature sensor reading does not change plausibly during warm-up, or its value disagrees with the intake air temperature when the engine has been off long enough that they should match. Often caused by a sensor that reports near a fixed value despite engine warm-up.
P0116.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Range/Performance

P0117.description: The ECT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot coolant temperature (typical NTC sensor characteristic — low resistance at high temperature).
P0117.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Low Input

common_causes: Open circuit in sensor or wiring
P0118.description: The ECT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold temperature (open-circuit-like behaviour). When this code is active, the ECU runs a default cold-start enrichment that wastes fuel and may cause black smoke.
P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor High Input

common_causes: Wiring chafed near hot engine parts
P0119.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. Fault not constantly present, typically due to loose connector, chafed wiring or a sensor failing thermally.
P0119.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent

P011A.description: ECT sensors 1 and 2 readings disagree beyond plausible limits — typically near startup both should match within tolerance.
P011A.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation

P011B.description: ECT and IAT readings disagree at long soak (engine off for hours) when both should match ambient. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P011B.title: Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation

P011C.description: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 1 disagree at long soak. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P011C.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 1

P011D.description: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 2 disagree at long soak. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
P011D.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 2

P011E.description: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.
P011E.title: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation

P011F.description: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.
P011F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation

common_causes: TPS worn or failed (dead spot in resistive track)
TPS mechanically misaligned to throttle shaft
P0120.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the throttle position sensor/switch A circuit. Signal missing, implausible, or wiring broken. Generic catch-all when no more specific TPS-A code applies.
P0120.title: Throttle Position Sensor / Switch A Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: TPS contact track worn (older potentiometer-type sensors)
P0121.description: The throttle position sensor (TPS) signal does not match the expected range for the commanded pedal position. On drive-by-wire vehicles, two redundant sensors are compared; a divergence between them or implausible motion triggers this code.
P0121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Range/Performance

P0122.description: The TPS signal voltage is below the lower acceptable threshold. The ECU usually enters limp-home mode and limits engine torque while the fault is active.
P0122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Low Input

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
P0123.description: The TPS signal voltage exceeds the upper acceptable threshold. As with P0122, limp-home mode is typical until the fault clears.
P0123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" High Input

common_causes: Sensor track worn at one spot (older potentiometer-type)
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0124.description: The TPS signal shows intermittent dropouts that do not stay outside threshold long enough to trigger P0122/P0123. Drive-by-wire systems are sensitive to this and may briefly enter limp-home mode each time.
P0124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent

P0125.description: The engine has run long enough that closed-loop fuel control should be active, but the coolant temperature has not risen high enough. Often caused by a stuck-open thermostat or a failed coolant temperature sensor.
P0125.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control

P0126.description: Coolant temperature stays below the value expected for stable engine operation. Almost always points to a thermostat stuck open or a sensor reading lower than the actual engine temperature.
P0126.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation

P0127.description: Intake air temperature exceeds the safe maximum. Risk of preignition or knock; ECU may reduce power.
P0127.title: Intake Air Temperature Too High

P0128.description: The engine has been running long enough to reach operating temperature, but coolant temperature stayed below the thermostat's regulating value. Almost always caused by a thermostat stuck open. Costs fuel economy and increases cold-engine emissions.
P0128.title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature

P0129.description: Barometric pressure reading below the plausible minimum. Either operating at extreme altitude or sensor fault.
P0129.title: Barometric Pressure Too Low

P012A.description: Generic electrical fault on turbo/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P012A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P012B.description: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A reading implausible. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P012B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P012C.description: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P012C.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P012D.description: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P012D.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P012E.description: Intermittent signal from turbo inlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
P012E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P012F.description: Engine coolant and oil temperature readings disagree beyond plausible limits. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
P012F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature / Engine Oil Temperature Correlation

P0130.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an implausible signal — typically stuck mid-range, no switching between rich and lean, or no signal at all. Closed-loop fuel control cannot run while this fault is active.
P0130.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)

common_causes: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
Genuine lean running (vacuum leak, low fuel pressure)
P0131.description: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage, indicating the ECU sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 1 — or the sensor signal path is shorted to ground.
P0131.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)

common_causes: Genuine rich running (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor poisoned by silicone or coolant
P0132.description: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich exhaust on bank 1 or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.
P0132.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)

P0133.description: The upstream oxygen sensor switches between rich and lean too slowly. Aged sensors lose response speed before they fail outright; this code typically appears before P0130/P0131/P0132.
P0133.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response (Bank 1, Sensor 1)

common_causes: Sensor aged or poisoned (silicone, lead, coolant)
Exhaust leak upstream of sensor diluting reading
P0134.description: The ECU detects that the upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 shows no switching activity or responds too slowly to changing exhaust gas composition. Often the sensor is aged, contaminated by silicone or fuel additives, or the heater circuit is degraded.
P0134.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)

P0135.description: The heating element inside the upstream oxygen sensor draws no current, draws too much current, or is open-circuit. The heater brings the sensor to operating temperature so closed-loop control can start within seconds rather than minutes.
P0135.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)

P0136.description: A general fault has been detected in the downstream (post-catalyst) oxygen sensor on bank 1. The downstream sensor monitors catalyst efficiency rather than fuel mixture; with no signal, the catalyst monitor cannot run.
P0136.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)

common_causes: Exhaust leak between catalyst and downstream sensor
P0137.description: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage. Either the catalyst is letting unburned oxygen through (sensor sees lean), the sensor itself is shorted to ground, or the catalyst is so degraded that the downstream signal mirrors a lean upstream condition.
P0137.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0138.description: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich downstream reading (less common, since post-cat exhaust should be more stable) or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.
P0138.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)

common_causes: Engine running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Sensor signal wire shorted to voltage
P0139.description: The ECU detects that the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an abnormally high voltage signal, suggesting a persistently rich exhaust condition past the catalyst, a shorted sensor, or wiring shorted to a voltage source.
P0139.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

P013A.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. Sensor aging or contamination.
P013A.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2

P013B.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P013B.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2

P013C.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. Sensor aging or contamination.
P013C.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2

P013D.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P013D.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2

P013E.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P013E.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2

P013F.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P013F.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2

common_causes: Catalytic converter so degraded that downstream signal mirrors upstream
P0140.description: The ECU detects no switching or excessively slow response from the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1. Typical for an aged or poisoned sensor; downstream sensors should show a relatively flat signal but must respond to fueling changes during diagnostic monitor runs.
P0140.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

P0141.description: The heating element inside the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 is open-circuit, drawing no current, or drawing too much. Without heater, the sensor takes much longer to reach operating temperature, delaying catalyst diagnosis.
P0141.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)

P0142.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1. The heater current is out of range, suggesting an open or shorted heater element, blown fuse or wiring fault.
P0142.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

P0143.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third oxygen sensor in the bank 1 exhaust path (typically located after a second catalyst on diesel or large engines with multi-cat exhausts).
P0143.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)

common_causes: Lean exhaust (vacuum leak, low fuel pressure)
P0144.description: The ECU detects an abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Indicates persistently lean exhaust, an open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
P0144.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)

common_causes: Rich exhaust (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
P0145.description: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Indicates persistently rich exhaust, a shorted sensor or wiring shorted to a voltage source.
P0145.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)

P0146.description: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Typical for aged or poisoned sensor.
P0146.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 3)

P0147.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Heater current out of range, indicating open/shorted heater element, blown fuse or wiring fault.
P0147.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)

P0148.description: Fuel quantity actually delivered does not match the commanded value over a long observation window. Mechanical issue in the fuel system.
P0148.title: Fuel Delivery Error

P0149.description: Injection timing deviates from target. Often caused by chain wear, sensor offset, or injector response drift.
P0149.title: Fuel Timing Error

P014A.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P014A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2

P014B.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P014B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2

P014C.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P014C.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1

P014D.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P014D.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1

P014E.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P014E.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1

P014F.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P014F.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1

P0150.description: Same condition as P0130 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine. Closed-loop fuel control on bank 2 is disabled while this fault is active.
P0150.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)

common_causes: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
Bank 2 running lean (vacuum leak, fuel pressure)
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0151.description: Same condition as P0131 but on bank 2. The upstream sensor sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 2 or has a signal short to ground.
P0151.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)

common_causes: Bank 2 running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0152.description: Same condition as P0132 but on bank 2. The upstream sensor reports a continuously rich condition or has a short to supply voltage.
P0152.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)

common_causes: Bank 2 running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
P0153.description: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently rich exhaust, shorted sensor or wiring shorted to voltage.
P0153.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)

P0154.description: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Typically aged or poisoned sensor, weak heater, or upstream exhaust leak.
P0154.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1)

P0155.description: Same condition as P0135 but on the upstream sensor of bank 2. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0155.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)

P0156.description: Same condition as P0136 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2. The catalyst efficiency monitor for bank 2 cannot run while this fault is active.
P0156.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)

P0157.description: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently lean exhaust past the catalyst, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
P0157.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0158.description: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 (alternate definition mapping in some manufacturers' interpretation). Indicates persistent lean reading, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
P0158.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0159.description: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently rich exhaust past the cat, shorted sensor or wiring shorted to voltage.
P0159.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

P015A.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P015A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1

P015B.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P015B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1

P015C.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P015C.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1

P015D.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P015D.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1

P015E.description: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop control of fuel injection timing. Often slow sensor warm-up.
P015E.title: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Fuel Timing Control

P015F.description: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop cylinder balance control.
P015F.title: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Cylinder Balance Control

P0160.description: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Often aged or poisoned sensor; downstream sensors usually flat but must respond on diagnostic monitor runs.
P0160.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

P0161.description: Same condition as P0141 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
P0161.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)

P0162.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Heater current out of range — open or shorted heater element, blown fuse, or wiring fault.
P0162.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 2)

P0163.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third O2 sensor in the bank 2 exhaust path (typically post-second-cat in multi-cat exhausts).
P0163.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0164.description: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates lean exhaust, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
P0164.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0165.description: The ECU detects abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates rich exhaust or wiring shorted to voltage.
P0165.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

P0166.description: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Typically aged or poisoned sensor or weak heater.
P0166.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

P0167.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Heater current out of range — open or shorted heater, blown fuse, wiring fault.
P0167.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

P0168.description: Fuel temperature exceeds the safe maximum. Risk of fuel pump damage and injection imprecision.
P0168.title: Fuel Temperature Too High

common_causes: Wrong fuel filled (e.g. E85 in non-flex)
P0169.description: Fuel composition (e.g. ethanol fraction on flex-fuel vehicles) outside expected range. Wrong fuel filled or sensor fault.
P0169.title: Incorrect Fuel Composition

P016A.description: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop air/fuel ratio control. Most often O2 sensor heater aging or coolant temperature reading wrong.
P016A.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control

P016B.description: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its lean correction limit because mixture is structurally too rich. Likely fuel pressure too high, leaking injector, or O2 sensor reporting too lean.
P016B.title: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Rich

P016C.description: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its rich correction limit because mixture is structurally too lean. Likely vacuum leak, low fuel pressure, or contaminated MAF.
P016C.title: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Lean

P016D.description: ECU took longer than allowed to close the loop on fuel pressure control. Pressure rise too slow at start.
P016D.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control

P016E.description: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its lower limit because rail pressure is structurally too high.
P016E.title: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too High

P016F.description: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its upper limit because rail pressure is structurally too low.
P016F.title: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too Low

common_causes: Fuel pressure too low or too high
P0170.description: The ECU detects that short-term and long-term fuel trim values on bank 1 are outside acceptable limits. Engine cannot maintain stoichiometric mixture — typically a vacuum leak, fuel pressure issue, or failing MAF/O2 sensor.
P0170.title: Fuel Trim Malfunction (Bank 1)

common_causes: Vacuum leak in intake or PCV system
P0171.description: Long-term fuel trim on bank 1 is at the upper limit — the ECU is adding more fuel than baseline to maintain stoichiometric mixture but cannot reach target. Indicates unmetered air entering the intake or insufficient fuel delivery.
P0171.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)

P0172.description: Long-term fuel trim on bank 1 is at the lower limit — the ECU is removing fuel from baseline but mixture remains too rich. Indicates excess fuel delivery, restricted air flow, or a faulty oxygen sensor reporting falsely lean.
P0172.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)

P0173.description: Fuel trims on bank 2 exceed adaptation limits in either lean or rich direction. The ECU cannot maintain stoichiometric mixture within calibrated boundaries.
P0173.title: Fuel Trim Malfunction Bank 2

common_causes: Central vacuum leak (intake manifold gasket, brake booster)
P0174.description: Same condition as P0171 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine (V6, V8, flat-six, etc.). When P0171 and P0174 appear together, the cause is usually a shared component such as the MAF sensor or a central vacuum leak rather than a bank-specific fault.
P0174.title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)

P0175.description: Same condition as P0172 but on bank 2. When paired with P0172, suspect shared causes (fuel pressure, blocked air filter); when alone, suspect a bank-specific injector or oxygen sensor.
P0175.title: System Too Rich (Bank 2)

P0176.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the flex-fuel composition sensor circuit. The sensor measures ethanol content (E0–E85) in the fuel; signal missing, shorted or out of plausible range.
P0176.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Malfunction

P0177.description: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not match expected values for the current fuel mix or rate-of-change is implausible.
P0177.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range / Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0178.description: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal is below the minimum threshold. Likely shorted to ground, open circuit or failed sensor.
P0178.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Low Input

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0179.description: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal exceeds the maximum threshold. Likely shorted to voltage, open ground or failed sensor.
P0179.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit High Input

P017A.description: Generic electrical fault on cylinder head temperature sensor A (CHT sensor — used on engines without conventional ECT).
P017A.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P017B.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P017C.description: CHT sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P017C.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P017D.description: CHT sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P017D.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P017E.description: Intermittent signal from CHT sensor A. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P017E.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P017F.description: Air filter on the EVAP leak detection pump module is restricted. Leak detection cannot establish reference pressure.
P017F.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Module Air Filter Restricted

P0180.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor A circuit. Fuel temperature input is missing or out of plausible range — typical for sensor failure or wiring open/short.
P0180.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Malfunction

P0181.description: The fuel temperature sensor A signal is within electrical limits but inconsistent with plausibility checks (e.g. doesn't change with engine warmup, disagrees with ambient temperature).
P0181.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range / Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0182.description: The fuel temperature sensor A signal is below the minimum threshold. Likely shorted to ground or open circuit.
P0182.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low Input

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0183.description: The fuel temperature sensor A signal exceeds the maximum threshold. Likely shorted to voltage, open ground or sensor open-circuit.
P0183.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit High Input

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0184.description: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the fuel temperature sensor A circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing thermally.
P0184.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

P0185.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor B circuit (second sensor used on systems with separate supply/return temperature monitoring or twin-tank arrangements).
P0185.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Malfunction

P0186.description: Fuel temperature sensor B reading is within electrical limits but implausible (no warmup change, disagrees with sensor A or ambient).
P0186.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range / Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0187.description: Fuel temperature sensor B signal below minimum. Shorted to ground or sensor open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0187.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low Input

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0188.description: Fuel temperature sensor B signal exceeds maximum. Shorted to voltage, open ground or open sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0188.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit High Input

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0189.description: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the fuel temperature sensor B circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing under thermal load.
P0189.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent

P018A.description: Generic electrical fault on fuel pressure sensor B (second sensor, e.g. low-pressure side or alternative fuel system).
P018A.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P018B.description: Fuel pressure sensor B reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P018B.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P018C.description: Fuel pressure sensor B signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P018C.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P018D.description: Fuel pressure sensor B signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P018D.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P018E.description: Intermittent signal from fuel pressure sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P018E.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P018F.description: The mechanical pressure relief valve has activated repeatedly within a short window — pressure regulation is failing more than once.
P018F.title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Frequent Activation

P0190.description: The ECU detects an out-of-range signal from the fuel rail pressure sensor. The voltage is outside calibrated min/max boundaries during normal operation.
P0190.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit

P0191.description: The fuel rail pressure sensor signal is within electrical limits but doesn't match commanded rail pressure under various engine loads. Common in common-rail diesel and GDI petrol engines.
P0191.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Range / Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0192.description: The ECU reads a voltage from the fuel rail pressure sensor below the calibrated minimum, indicating short to ground or open supply.
P0192.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0193.description: The ECU reads a voltage from the fuel rail pressure sensor above the calibrated maximum, indicating short to power or open ground reference.
P0193.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High Input

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0194.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the fuel rail pressure sensor. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing under vibration/heat.
P0194.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent

P0195.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault in the engine oil temperature sensor circuit. Signal missing, shorted or out of plausible range.
P0195.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Malfunction

P0196.description: Engine oil temperature sensor signal is within electrical limits but implausible (no warmup change, contradicts coolant temperature).
P0196.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Range / Performance

P0197.description: Engine oil temperature sensor signal below minimum. Shorted to ground or open.
P0197.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Low

P0198.description: Engine oil temperature sensor signal exceeds maximum. Shorted to voltage, open ground or open sensor.
P0198.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0199.description: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the engine oil temperature sensor circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing thermally.
P0199.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Intermittent

P019A.description: Bank 1 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during rich-to-lean transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P019A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 3

P019B.description: Bank 1 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during lean-to-rich transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P019B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 3

P019C.description: Bank 2 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during rich-to-lean transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P019C.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 3

P019D.description: Bank 2 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during lean-to-rich transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
P019D.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 3

P019E.description: Generic electrical fault on alternative fuel tank A pressure sensor (CNG, LPG, hydrogen).
P019E.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant
P019F.description: Alternative fuel tank A pressure reading implausible.
P019F.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P01A0.description: Alt fuel tank A pressure sensor signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P01A0.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P01A1.description: Alt fuel tank A pressure sensor signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P01A1.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit High

P02F5.title: Cylinder 8 Injector Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02FA.description: The diesel intake throttle position sensor does not reach the calibrated minimum or maximum stop value during a self-test sweep — typically sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a sticky throttle plate.
P02FA.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P02FB.description: The drive circuit for the cold-start auxiliary fuel injector or the cold-start ECU output is open. Some diesels use an extra cold-start injector to inject fuel into the intake manifold during very cold starts.
P02FB.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P02FC.description: Cold-start injector drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P02FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P02FD.description: Cold-start injector drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P02FD.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit High

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P02FE.description: Cold-start injector drive is electrically OK but does not deliver the calibrated injection quantity — partial blockage or weak coil.
P02FE.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit Range/Performance

P02FF.description: The timer that monitors how long the propulsion system has been inactive (used by hybrid and stop-start strategies to schedule rebalancing tasks) is not behaving plausibly — typically a clock or PCM-state fault.
P02FF.title: Propulsion System Inactive Timer Performance

P0300.description: The ECU has detected misfires that are not concentrated on a single cylinder. The misfire monitor measures crankshaft acceleration after each combustion event; missing acceleration on multiple cylinders, or randomly across cylinders, triggers this code.
P0300.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected

common_causes: Spark plug for cylinder 1 worn or fouled
P0301.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 1. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0301.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected

common_causes: Spark plug for cylinder 2 worn or fouled
P0302.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 2. Diagnostic approach is identical to P0301 — swap the suspect coil or plug with a known-good cylinder and see if the misfire follows.
P0302.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected

common_causes: Spark plug for cylinder 3 worn or fouled
P0303.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 3. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. Verify by swapping the suspected coil/plug to a different cylinder; if the code follows, the part is bad.
P0303.title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected

common_causes: Spark plug for cylinder 4 worn or fouled
P0304.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 4. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. Verify by swapping the suspected coil/plug to a different cylinder; if the code follows, the part is bad.
P0304.title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected

P0305.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 5 (only present on engines with 5+ cylinders). Same diagnostic approach as P0301 — swap the suspect coil/plug with another cylinder.
P0305.title: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected

P0306.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 6. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression. Verify by swapping the suspected coil/plug to a different cylinder; if the code follows, the part is bad.
P0306.title: Cylinder 6 Misfire Detected

P0307.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 7. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0307.title: Cylinder 7 Misfire Detected

P0308.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 8. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0308.title: Cylinder 8 Misfire Detected

P0309.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 9. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0309.title: Cylinder 9 Misfire Detected

common_causes: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P030A.description: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open: the circuit is open. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.
P030A.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P030B.description: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.
P030B.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P030C.description: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. This line drives an ignition coil group; a fault causes misfire on those cylinders.
P030C.title: Ignition A Control Signal Circuit High

common_causes: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P030D.description: The ignition B control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.
P030D.title: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P030E.description: Ignition B control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P030E.title: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P030F.description: Ignition B control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P030F.title: Ignition B Control Signal Circuit High

P0310.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 10. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0310.title: Cylinder 10 Misfire Detected

P0311.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 11. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0311.title: Cylinder 11 Misfire Detected

P0312.description: Misfires concentrated on cylinder 12. A cylinder-specific code points away from shared causes (fuel pressure, MAF) toward components dedicated to that cylinder — coil, spark plug, injector, compression.
P0312.title: Cylinder 12 Misfire Detected

P0313.description: Misfires are detected while the fuel level is low. The ECM disables further misfire reporting under this condition because intermittent fuel starvation can cause false positives in catalyst-damaging logic.
P0313.title: Misfire Detected with Low Fuel

common_causes: Weak ignition component on one cylinder
P0314.description: A persistent misfire is detected on one cylinder, but the engine controller cannot identify which cylinder is affected. Often seen on engines without per-cylinder feedback or when crank position correlation fails.
P0314.title: Single Cylinder Misfire — Cylinder Not Specified

P0315.description: The PCM has not yet learned the crankshaft position variation table required for accurate misfire detection. After flywheel/sensor replacement or PCM relearn, a procedure must be performed (typically deceleration from a defined RPM with closed throttle).
P0315.title: Crankshaft Position System Variation Not Learned

common_causes: Ignition coil weak below operating temperature
Cold-start mixture too lean (fuel pressure, leaking injectors at rest)
P0316.description: The misfire monitor detected misfires during the first 1000 revolutions after startup but the engine then settled. Often caused by fouled spark plugs that warm up clean, weak ignition coils, or a borderline cold-start fuel mixture.
P0316.title: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)

common_causes: PCM configuration does not match installed hardware
P0317.description: The PCM has been configured to use rough-road sensor input for misfire detection (to mask false positives on bumpy surfaces) but the expected hardware is not detected on the network. Typically a configuration mismatch after replacement.
P0317.title: Rough Road Hardware Not Present

P0318.description: A general electrical fault is reported on rough-road sensor A — used to gate misfire detection so that engine vibration from rough roads is not misclassified as misfire.
P0318.title: Rough Road Sensor A Signal Circuit

P0319.description: A general electrical fault is reported on rough-road sensor B — used to gate misfire detection so that engine vibration from rough roads is not misclassified as misfire.
P0319.title: Rough Road Sensor B Signal Circuit

common_causes: Open wire between PCM and coil
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P031A.description: The ignition C control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.
P031A.title: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P031B.description: Ignition C control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P031B.title: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P031C.description: Ignition C control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P031C.title: Ignition C Control Signal Circuit High
