Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P031D.description: The ignition D control signal circuit is open — typically the PCM drive line for the first ignition coil group has lost continuity.
P031D.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P031E.description: Ignition D control signal stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P031E.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P031F.description: Ignition D control signal stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P031F.title: Ignition D Control Signal Circuit High

P0320.description: A general electrical fault is reported on the engine speed input from the ignition/distributor — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. On older systems this is the distributor pickup; on newer ones it is the crank/cam-derived speed signal feeding the ignition driver.
P0320.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit

common_causes: Sensor drift or pickup gap wrong
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0321.description: Engine speed input from the ignition/distributor is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — slow response, drift, or noise.
P0321.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Pickup dead or air gap excessive
P0322.description: No engine speed signal from the ignition/distributor — open circuit, dead pickup, or sensor air gap too wide.
P0322.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0323.description: Engine speed input signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or wiring issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0323.title: Ignition/Distributor Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P0324.description: The knock-control subsystem reports an internal error — typically a self-test fault or a noise floor that cannot be calibrated. The system protects against detonation by retarding ignition; with this fault knock control is disabled.
P0324.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Control System Error

common_causes: Sensor mounting bolt loose (sensor must be torqued correctly)
P0325.description: A general fault has been detected in the bank 1 knock sensor circuit. The ECU uses the knock sensor to detect pre-ignition and retards ignition timing when knock occurs; with no signal, the ECU runs conservative timing and loses power.
P0325.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1)

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
P0326.description: Knock sensor A signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.
P0326.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0327.description: The knock sensor signal voltage is below the expected range. Usually points to a piezoelectric sensor that has lost its output, or a short to ground in the signal line.
P0327.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)

common_causes: Mechanical noise picked up by sensor (loose accessory)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
P0328.description: The knock sensor signal voltage is above the expected range. Often caused by a sensor producing excess output due to mechanical noise (loose mounting, accessory drive vibration) rather than a sensor fault.
P0328.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit High Input (Bank 1)

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P0329.description: Knock sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.
P0329.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P032A.description: A general electrical fault on knock sensor C — used on engines with multiple knock sensors (one per bank or per cylinder pair).
P032A.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P032B.description: Knock sensor C signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.
P032B.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P032C.description: Knock sensor C signal below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P032C.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Low

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P032D.description: Knock sensor C signal above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P032D.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit High

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P032E.description: Knock sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.
P032E.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor C Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Low compression on one or more cylinders
P032F.description: The engine torque measured (or modelled from intake/exhaust signals) is below the calibrated set point for the commanded throttle position. Causes range from low compression, intake leak, fuel pressure issue, ignition fault, to high mechanical drag.
P032F.title: Combustion Engine Producing Insufficient Torque

P0330.description: A general electrical fault in the bank 2 knock sensor circuit. The ECU monitors a piezoelectric sensor for engine vibration patterns associated with detonation; an open, shorted, or out-of-range circuit triggers this code.
P0330.title: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit (Bank 2)

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P0331.description: Knock sensor B signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.
P0331.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0332.description: Knock sensor 2 (bank 2) reports a signal level below the diagnostic threshold. The sensor is a piezo element bolted to the engine block; output should be a small AC voltage on each combustion event. A cold or open sensor reads 0 V; a loose mounting bolt damps the signal. Without knock detection, the ECM retards spark globally as a safety measure — fuel economy and power suffer.
P0332.title: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit Low Input (Bank 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0333.description: The bank 2 knock sensor signal is above the expected voltage range. Typically caused by a short to supply voltage or an internal sensor fault.
P0333.title: Knock Sensor 2 Circuit High Input (Bank 2)

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P0334.description: Knock sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.
P0334.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor B Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Reluctor ring damaged or contaminated with metal debris
P0335.description: The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor signal is missing or implausible. The CKP is essential — without it the ECU cannot synchronise injection or ignition, and the engine will not start or will stall.
P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Malfunction

P0336.description: The CKP signal is present but inconsistent with engine RPM, or pulse counts deviate from the reluctor's expected pattern. Often points to a damaged tooth on the reluctor or an air gap that has changed.
P0336.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0337.description: The CKP signal voltage is below the lower threshold. Usually a sensor whose internal coil has degraded, or a wiring short to ground.
P0337.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0338.description: The CKP signal voltage is above the upper threshold. Either a sensor producing excess output or a short to supply voltage.
P0338.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit High Input

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0339.description: The crankshaft position sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector, sensor air gap, or damaged tone wheel. The PCM may detect a "false" stall or misfire spike when the signal drops.
P0339.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P033A.description: A general electrical fault on knock sensor D — used on engines with multiple knock sensors (one per bank or per cylinder pair).
P033A.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P033B.description: Knock sensor D signal is in electrical range but plausibility check fails — typically a loose mounting, wrong torque, or sensor element drift.
P033B.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P033C.description: Knock sensor D signal below lower plausibility — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P033C.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Low

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P033D.description: Knock sensor D signal above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P033D.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit High

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P033E.description: Knock sensor D signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually a corroded connector or chafed wire near the cylinder head.
P033E.title: Knock/Combustion Vibration Sensor D Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Crank or cam sensor signal corrupted
P033F.description: The PCM has lost crank-to-cam synchronization — the relative phase between crankshaft and camshaft no longer matches the calibrated reference. Causes include a stretched or jumped timing chain, broken cam timing tooth, or sensor signal corruption.
P033F.title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Loss Of Synchronization

common_causes: Timing chain stretched, throwing off sensor timing
P0340.description: The camshaft position (CMP) sensor signal is missing or implausible. The ECU uses CMP together with CKP to identify cylinder phase for sequential injection and coil-on-plug ignition; without CMP the engine may run on group injection or fail to start.
P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)

P0341.description: The CMP signal is present but its phase relative to the crankshaft is outside tolerance. On engines with variable valve timing, this code often appears together with VVT solenoid faults.
P0341.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0342.description: The CMP signal voltage is below the lower threshold. Most often a sensor with degraded internal output or a short to ground.
P0342.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0343.description: The CMP signal voltage is above the upper threshold. Either excessive sensor output or a short to supply voltage.
P0343.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit High Input (Bank 1)

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0344.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 or Single Sensor): the signal is intermittent or erratic. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P0344.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)

P0345.description: General electrical fault in the bank 2 camshaft position sensor circuit. The ECU uses this signal together with the crank sensor for sequential injection and ignition timing.
P0345.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 2)

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0346.description: The bank 2 camshaft position sensor signal is present but does not match the crank reference correctly, or its pulse pattern is implausible.
P0346.title: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0347.description: Camshaft position sensor A on bank 2 reads below lower plausibility — short to ground. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
P0347.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Low (Bank 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0348.description: Camshaft position sensor A on bank 2 reads above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
P0348.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit High (Bank 2)

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0349.description: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2): the signal is intermittent or erratic. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P0349.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)

common_causes: Tone wheel misindexed or relearn pending
P034A.description: At engine start the crankshaft position reported by the sensor does not match the calibrated start window — typically a wrong tone-wheel installation, sensor air gap, or PCM not synchronised after a relearn.
P034A.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Start Position Incorrect

P034B.description: The crankshaft is rotating in the wrong direction relative to the expected reference — typically only seen on stop-start systems where the engine briefly counter-rotates after shutdown.
P034B.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor - Crankshaft Direction Incorrect

P034C.description: Some engines (notably Saab and some Mazda direct-injection units) use the spark plug as an ion-current sensor after spark to detect knock and misfire. This code reports a performance issue with the ion-sense input — typically a worn plug, loose secondary connection, or aged ion-sense module.
P034C.title: Ion Sense System Performance

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P0350.description: A general open-circuit fault has been detected on an ignition coil's primary or secondary winding (no specific cylinder identified). This code is set when the PCM cannot localise the fault to a single coil.
P0350.title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit/Open

common_causes: Coil primary winding open or shorted
P0351.description: An electrical fault is detected in both the primary and the secondary circuit of ignition coil A (cylinder 1). The ECU cannot drive the coil correctly, so the cylinder served by coil A misfires or does not fire at all. Causes: an open or shorted primary control wire, an internal coil winding fault, a failed igniter/driver, or wiring or connector damage at the coil.
P0351.title: Ignition Coil "A" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 1)

common_causes: Coil primary winding open or shorted
P0352.description: An electrical fault has been detected in the ignition coil circuit for cylinder 2 — open primary winding, short to ground, or short to supply. The ECU disables the coil to protect its driver and the cylinder misfires.
P0352.title: Ignition Coil "B" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 2)

common_causes: Coil primary winding open or shorted
P0353.description: An electrical fault has been detected in the ignition coil circuit for cylinder 3 — open primary winding, short to ground, or short to supply. The ECU disables the coil to protect its driver and the cylinder misfires.
P0353.title: Ignition Coil "C" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 3)

common_causes: Coil primary winding open or shorted
P0354.description: An electrical fault has been detected in the ignition coil circuit for cylinder 4 — open primary winding, short to ground, or short to supply. The ECU disables the coil to protect its driver and the cylinder misfires.
P0354.title: Ignition Coil "D" Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 4)

P0355.description: An electrical fault is detected in both the primary and the secondary circuit of ignition coil E. The ECU cannot drive the coil correctly, so the cylinder served by coil E misfires or does not fire at all. Causes: an open or shorted primary control wire, an internal coil winding fault, a failed igniter/driver, or wiring or connector damage at the coil.
P0355.title: Ignition Coil "E" Primary/Secondary Circuit

P0356.description: An electrical fault is detected in both the primary and the secondary circuit of ignition coil F. P0400.description: A general fault has been detected in the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system. EGR routes a portion of exhaust back into the intake to reduce combustion temperature and NOx emissions. Most EGR codes today are caused by carbon buildup blocking the valve.
P0400.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Malfunction

common_causes: EGR valve clogged or stuck closed
Intake EGR passages blocked with carbon
Vacuum line to EGR (vacuum-actuated valves) cracked
P0401.description: When the ECU commands EGR open, the actual flow measured by the DPFE sensor or the resulting MAP/MAF change is below threshold. By far the most common cause is a carboned-up EGR valve or blocked intake passages.
P0401.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected

common_causes: Valve seat eroded — does not seal
P0402.description: EGR flow is higher than expected when the valve should be closed, or higher than commanded when partially open. Typically a valve that has stuck open due to carbon, causing rough idle and stalling.
P0402.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected

P0403.description: The control circuit for the EGR valve solenoid is open or shorted. The ECM cannot drive the valve to the commanded position.
P0403.title: EGR Control Circuit

P0404.description: The EGR valve does not move through its expected range or its position feedback does not track command. The valve may be sticking, the position sensor may be drifting or carbon buildup is preventing full travel.
P0404.title: EGR Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0405.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.
P0405.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0406.description: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.
P0406.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor "A" Circuit High

P0407.description: The signal from EGR position or pressure sensor B is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates a short to ground, open signal wire or sensor fault.

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P040A.description: A general electrical fault on EGR temperature sensor A — open, shorted, or out of plausibility. The sensor monitors recirculated exhaust gas temperature for EGR cooler protection and dosing.
P040A.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P040B.description: EGR temperature sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.
P040B.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P040C.description: EGR temperature sensor A below lower plausibility — short to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P040C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P040D.description: EGR temperature sensor A above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P040D.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P040E.description: EGR temperature sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P040E.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P040F.description: EGR temperature sensors A and B disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P040F.title: EGR Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation

common_causes: Air pump seized (water ingress is a common cause)
P0410.description: A general fault in the secondary air injection system. The system pumps fresh air into the exhaust during cold start to accelerate catalyst light-off; common faults are a seized pump, blocked passages or a stuck valve.
P0410.title: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction

common_causes: Air passages in cylinder head clogged with carbon
P0411.description: When the ECU commands secondary air injection, the actual flow measured by the front oxygen sensor (or a dedicated mass flow meter) does not match the expected value. Usually a partially blocked passage or a leaking combi valve.
P0411.title: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow

P0412.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.
P0412.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P0413.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Open: the circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed component.
P0413.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit Open

P0414.description: The ECU detected a short circuit in the secondary air injection switching valve A control circuit. With the valve unable to switch correctly, the cold-start emissions strategy fails and the catalyst takes longer to reach light-off.
P0414.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve "A" Circuit Shorted

P0415.description: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0419.description: A general electrical fault on AIR system control circuit B (typically the AIR pump driver line on the second pump or relay).

P041C.title: EGR Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P041D.description: EGR temperature sensor B above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

P0440.description: A general fault in the evaporative emission (EVAP) system has been detected. The system seals the fuel tank and captures fuel vapour in a charcoal canister; this code indicates a failed leak test or sensor without identifying the specific failure.
P0440.title: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction

common_causes: Purge valve stuck open or closed
P0441.description: The actual purge flow does not match the commanded value. Usually a purge valve stuck closed (no flow) or stuck open (too much flow at idle). Distinct from a leak code.
P0441.title: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow

common_causes: Fuel cap loose, missing, or worn seal
P0442.description: A small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.040 inch / 1.0 mm orifice) has been detected in the EVAP system. By far the most common cause is a fuel cap that is loose, missing, or has a worn seal.
P0442.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)

P0443.description: Electrical fault in the EVAP purge solenoid circuit. The ECU detects an open, shorted, or out-of-range condition on the purge valve driver.
P0443.title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P0444.description: The ECU has detected an open circuit in the purge solenoid control line — usually a broken wire, unplugged connector, or open coil winding.
P0444.title: Evaporative Emission Purge Control Valve Circuit Open

P0445.description: The ECU detected a short in the EVAP purge solenoid control circuit. With the valve permanently energized or shorted, the system can either over-purge causing rich running, or stay closed.
P0445.title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted

common_causes: Vent valve seized or contaminated by water/dirt
P0446.description: A fault in the EVAP vent valve circuit. The vent valve seals the canister against atmosphere during the leak test; without it, the test cannot pull a vacuum and may set false leak codes alongside.
P0446.title: Evaporative Emission Vent Control Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P0447.description: The ECU detected an open circuit on the EVAP vent valve control. The vent valve is needed to seal the system for leak diagnostics; with the circuit open the leak test cannot complete.
P0447.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Open

P0448.description: EVAP vent valve drive circuit shorted to ground or B+. The vent valve seals the canister during pressure-test diagnostics.
P0448.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Shorted

P0449.description: A general electrical fault was detected in the EVAP vent valve/solenoid control circuit. Without a working vent valve the EVAP leak test cannot complete and the system may remain not-ready.
P0449.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit Malfunction

P0451.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor reading is implausible — for example, fluctuating signal, noise, or values that do not respond to known pressure events such as a key-on tank refill.

P04DD.description: During the cold-start strategy the ECU briefly opens EGR A to slow combustion temperatures and reduce engine-out NOx during catalyst light-off. The measured EGR flow stays below the calibrated target despite the requested opening - typically a stuck-closed valve, restricted cold-start path, or sensor offset that under-reports flow.
P04DD.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected

common_causes: EGR valve A sticking open when cold
P04DE.description: Same as P04DD with EGR flow above the cold-start target - typically valve sticking open during the cold phase or position sensor offset low.
P04DE.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Excessive Detected

common_causes: Debris on valve seat prevents full closing
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P04DF.description: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.
P04DF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P04E0.description: Same as P04AF on EVAP purge valve A. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
P04E0.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed

P04E1.description: A dedicated sensor monitors whether the PCV hose is fitted to its connector at the engine. The ECU detects a circuit fault on this sensor - cannot determine whether the hose is connected. Required by some emissions regulations to flag a disconnected PCV hose immediately.
P04E1.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P04E2.description: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P04E2.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P04E3.description: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P04E3.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P04E4.description: Same as P04E1 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P04E4.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic

common_causes: Open in sensor signal, supply or ground
P04E5.description: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Without valid EGR feedback the ECU disables exhaust gas recirculation and may set further EGR codes.
P04E5.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit

P04E6.description: Same as P04CF on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P04E6.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range or Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P04E7.description: Same as P04D0 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P04E7.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P04E8.description: Same as P04D1 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P04E8.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P04E9.description: Same as P04D2 on EGR temperature sensor D. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.
P04E9.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent or Erratic

P04EA.description: The EVAP leak diagnostic has detected a small leak on the fuel tank side of the system - typically a hose, gasket, fuel cap, or fuel sender flange that does not seal completely. Vapor escapes during pressure or vacuum tests.
P04EA.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side

common_causes: Vent valve does not seal in test mode
P04EB.description: Same as P04EA but on the fresh-air side - the path between vent valve and atmosphere is not sealing completely during the active test phase.
P04EB.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side

common_causes: Fuel cap missing or not seated
Vapor hose pulled off or torn
P04EC.description: Same as P04EA but the leak is large enough that the system cannot build the test pressure or vacuum at all - typically a missing fuel cap, an unseated hose or a torn vapor line on the tank side.
P04EC.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side

P04ED.description: Same as P04EB on the fresh-air side, but with a leak large enough to prevent test build-up. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.
P04ED.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fresh Air Side

common_causes: Fuel cap O-ring aged or stiffened
P04EE.description: Same as P04EA but at the most sensitive leak threshold - typically the OBD-II 0.020-inch (~0.5 mm) test. The system holds pressure for some time but loses it slower than the diagnostic limit allows; usually fuel cap O-ring fatigue or microcracks in a hose.
P04EE.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side

P04EF.description: Same as P04EE on the fresh-air side - microcrack in a hose or imperfect vent valve seal at the most sensitive test threshold.
P04EF.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side

common_causes: Line, venturi or check valve restricted
P04F0.description: On engines that have a separate high-load purge line - to use boost pressure to pull vapor on turbo applications - the ECU monitors flow when this path is commanded. The flow is below the expected level - the venturi, line, or check valve is restricted, or the line is incorrectly routed.
P04F0.title: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance

P04F1.description: A general performance fault on the EVAP purge line - flow does not match the requested rate, without specifying which segment. Usually a partially blocked line, a stuck purge valve, or a leak that decouples flow from valve commands.
P04F1.title: EVAP System Purge Line Performance

common_causes: Heater supply voltage low or unstable
DC/DC converter fault on heater rail
P04F2.description: The electric catalyst heater on bank 1 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window. The heater cannot deliver the rated power, so cold-start emissions rise until the catalyst reaches light-off conventionally.
P04F2.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 1

common_causes: Heater supply voltage low or unstable
DC/DC converter fault on heater rail
P04F3.description: The electric catalyst heater on bank 2 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window. The heater cannot deliver the rated power, so cold-start emissions rise until the catalyst reaches light-off conventionally.
P04F3.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 2

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P04F4.description: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 1 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.
P04F4.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P04F5.description: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 2 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.
P04F5.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 2

common_causes: Open in heater element or harness
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P04F6.description: Same as P04F4 with the line shorted to supply or open - the ECU measures higher voltage than the commanded duty cycle allows.
P04F6.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P04F7.description: Same as P04F6 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P04F7.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 2

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P04F8.description: Same as P04F4 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the heater feed.
P04F8.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 1

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P04F9.description: Same as P04F8 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P04F9.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 2

common_causes: Actuator overheated due to nearby exhaust heat or duty-cycle stress
Cooling jacket or air flow insufficient
P04FA.description: The ECU monitors the operating temperature of the EGR A actuator (or its control electronics). The reading has exceeded the safe upper threshold and the control unit derates or disables EGR A to protect the actuator from thermal damage.
P04FA.title: EGR A Control Temperature Too High

P04FB.description: The sensor that monitors PCV hose connection reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with the engine model - signal does not switch when the hose is moved during diagnosis, or shows offset against actual hose state.
P04FB.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range or Performance

common_causes: Excessive blow-by from worn piston rings
P04FC.description: A general performance fault of the crankcase ventilation system - PCV pressure or flow does not match the engine model. Possible causes are a clogged PCV valve, blocked separator, oil-filler cap with a damaged seal, or excessive blow-by from worn rings.
P04FC.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Performance

common_causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P04FD.description: Modern smart EGR actuators contain their own microcontroller that handles position control internally and reports back over LIN or PWM. The ECU detects implausible behaviour from the actuator processor - missed messages, incorrect responses, or watchdog resets.
P04FD.title: EGR Actuator A Control Processor Performance

common_causes: Heater element aged - reduced power output
P04FE.description: The catalyst heater on bank 1 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated. Heater element ageing, increased contact resistance, or a partial winding failure are typical causes.
P04FE.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 1

common_causes: Heater element aged - reduced power output
P04FF.description: The catalyst heater on bank 2 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated. Heater element ageing, increased contact resistance, or a partial winding failure are typical causes.
P04FF.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 2

P0500.description: The vehicle speed sensor (VSS) signal is missing or implausible. On automatic transmissions this often disables cruise control and shift adaptation; ABS-equipped cars typically derive speed from wheel speed sensors as a fallback.
P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Malfunction

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0501.description: The VSS signal is present but inconsistent — either values jump implausibly or the sensor reports a speed inconsistent with engine RPM in gear. Often a damaged reluctor ring or a sensor with degraded magnetic response.
P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0502.description: The primary vehicle speed sensor (VSS A) reports a signal voltage below the plausible lower limit. With no usable speed signal the ECU loses cruise control, gear-shift logic and certain anti-stall functions.
P0502.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Noise on signal line or intermittent open
Reluctor ring damaged or missing teeth
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0503.description: Same as P0502 with the signal noisy, erratic or above the plausible upper limit - typical for a chafed harness, missing reluctor tooth or a sensor with a weakened magnet.
P0503.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Erratic or High

P0504.description: Modern vehicles use two redundant brake switch signals (often one normally-open and one normally-closed). When the two signals disagree, this code is set; common causes include a misadjusted switch, internal switch failure, or wiring fault.
P0504.title: Brake Switch "A"/"B" Correlation

P0505.description: A general fault has been detected in the idle air control (IAC) system. On older vehicles with a separate IAC valve, this means the valve cannot maintain commanded idle RPM; on drive-by-wire systems, the equivalent fault is in the throttle body's idle adaptation.
P0505.title: Idle Air Control System Malfunction

common_causes: Throttle body or idle bypass passage clogged
P0506.description: The engine idles below the target RPM despite the IAC opening fully. Indicates restricted air path past the IAC — typically a heavily fouled throttle body or stuck IAC valve.
P0506.title: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected

P0507.description: Idle RPM exceeds the target despite the IAC commanded fully closed. Almost always caused by a vacuum leak that lets air bypass the IAC — torn intake hose, leaking PCV, brake booster, or intake manifold gasket.
P0507.title: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0508.description: The control line to the idle air control valve - which opens a small bypass around the throttle to set idle airflow - is shorted to ground or measures a voltage below the plausible level.
P0508.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low

common_causes: Open in IAC valve or harness
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0509.description: Same as P0508 with the line shorted to supply or open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0509.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit High

common_causes: Intake leak only when cold (gasket shrinks)
P050A.description: During the cold-start phase the ECU runs an elevated idle speed and a richer mixture to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature quickly. The cold-start idle does not behave as commanded - speed sags, hunts, or fails to come up. Possible causes are intake leaks active when cold, an IAC valve sticking, or implausible coolant temperature.
P050A.title: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance

common_causes: Knock sensor drift causes wrong feedback
P050B.description: During cold-start the ECU retards ignition timing to raise exhaust temperature for catalyst light-off. The strategy does not deliver the expected timing - feedback from knock sensor or combustion model shows ignition too far advanced or retarded for the demanded calibration.
P050B.title: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance

common_causes: Thermostat stuck open - engine warms too slowly
P050C.description: During cold-start the ECU expects coolant temperature to rise within a calibrated time window. Either the engine warms up too slowly (stuck-open thermostat, weak combustion) or the temperature signal does not reflect the actual warm-up.
P050C.title: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance

common_causes: Injector tip coked - poor cold spray pattern
P050D.description: The ECU detects rough idle behaviour during the cold-start phase only. Once the engine has warmed up the issue disappears. Typically caused by injector deposits, low compression on one cylinder when cold, or sticky valve guides.
P050D.title: Cold Start Rough Idle

common_causes: Excessive heat loss between port and catalyst
P050E.description: During the cold-start strategy the ECU monitors exhaust temperature to ensure catalyst light-off. The measured EGT remains below the target threshold within the allowed time - heat-up strategy is not effective. Causes include excessive heat loss, very rich mixture cooling the exhaust, or a faulty EGT sensor.
P050E.title: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low

common_causes: Vacuum leak in booster line or check valve
P050F.description: The ECU monitors the vacuum supplied to the brake booster (either via a dedicated sensor or via intake manifold pressure). The level has dropped below the calibrated threshold; brake-pedal feel will be hard, and an electric vacuum pump may be commanded to restore vacuum.
P050F.title: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low

common_causes: Switch out of adjustment or worn
P0510.description: The dedicated closed-throttle switch (or closed-throttle bit on the TPS) does not behave as expected - either it never activates, never deactivates, or shows incoherent state against TPS voltage and engine load. Used by older systems for fuel-cutoff and idle recognition.
P0510.title: Closed Throttle Position Switch

P0511.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the idle air control valve - open or short on supply, signal or ground. The ECU loses control of idle bypass airflow.
P0511.title: Idle Air Control Circuit

P0512.description: The starter request input - the signal that tells the ECU the driver wants to crank the engine - shows a circuit fault. Without it the engine cannot be started under software-managed start strategies (stop-start, push-button, immobiliser-coordinated start).
P0512.title: Starter Request Circuit

P0513.description: The immobiliser system has detected a key that is not authorised for this vehicle. Engine start is blocked. Possible causes are an unprogrammed replacement key, a transponder fault, or a deliberate attempt to start with the wrong key.
P0513.title: Incorrect Immobilizer Key

P0514.description: The battery temperature sensor reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with engine bay or coolant temperature. Modern alternator regulation uses battery temperature to adjust charging voltage, so an offset here causes over- or undercharging.
P0514.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance

P0515.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the battery temperature sensor - open or short on supply, signal or ground.
P0515.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0516.description: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0516.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0517.description: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0517.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0518.description: Same as P0511 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0518.title: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: IAC valve sticking due to carbon
P0519.description: The idle air control system is electrically intact, but the actual idle airflow does not match the commanded value - typical for a sticky valve, intake leak, or carbon build-up around the throttle bore.
P0519.title: Idle Air Control System Performance

P051A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the crankcase pressure sensor A - typically used to monitor PCV operation and detect a clogged separator or disconnected hose.
P051A.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit

P051B.description: Same as P051A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.
P051B.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P051C.description: Same as P051A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P051C.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P051D.description: Same as P051A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P051D.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P051E.description: Same as P051A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P051E.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic

common_causes: PCV filter saturated with oil mist
P051F.description: The pressure or flow sensor in the PCV path detects increased restriction across the oil-mist filter element. Once saturated with oil mist, the filter no longer passes blow-by gas, raising crankcase pressure and pushing oil past seals.
P051F.title: PCV Filter Restriction

P0520.description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.
P0520.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0521.description: The engine oil pressure sensor or switch reports values that are not plausible for current RPM, oil temperature, and engine load. Could indicate a sensor fault or genuinely abnormal pressure.
P0521.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance

P0522.description: The oil pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum. Often points to an electrical fault — short to ground or failed sensor — but can also indicate genuinely low oil pressure.
P0522.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Low Voltage

P0523.description: Same as P0520 with the signal voltage above the plausible range - usually a short to supply or sensor failure that pegs the output high.
P0523.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A High

P0524.description: The ECU has determined that engine oil pressure is below the safe operating threshold. Caused by low oil level, worn oil pump, severe engine wear, or a stuck pressure relief valve. Continued operation can rapidly destroy the engine.
P0524.title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low

common_causes: Servo response slow due to wear
P0525.description: The control circuit to the cruise control servo (vacuum or electric actuator that holds throttle position) shows feedback in plausible range yet inconsistent with the commanded action - servo slow, sticking, or supply weak.
P0525.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range or Performance

P0526.description: A general circuit fault on the cooling fan tachometer feedback - the ECU loses fan speed information needed to verify cooling capacity and detect a stalled or runaway fan.
P0526.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit

P0527.description: Same as P0526 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the commanded fan speed - typically sensor drift, weak magnet, or partial reluctor damage.
P0527.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range or Performance

P0528.description: Same as P0526 with no detectable signal at all - sensor not producing pulses despite the fan being commanded on.
P0528.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0529.description: Same as P0526 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0529.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent

P052A.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P052A.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1

P052B.description: Same as P052A with the phaser stuck retarded - cold-start strategy cannot pull the cam to the advanced position needed for fast catalyst light-off.
P052B.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1

P052C.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.
P052C.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2

P052D.description: Same as P052B on bank 2. The camshaft position sensor identifies which cylinder is on the compression stroke — without it the ECM cannot run sequential injection or coil-on-plug ignition correctly.
P052D.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2

P052E.description: The crankcase ventilation regulator valve - which throttles blow-by gas flow toward the intake based on engine load - is electrically intact but does not deliver the modelled pressure regulation. Either the valve diaphragm is fatigued or the spring is weak.
P052E.title: PCV Regulator Valve Performance

P052F.description: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
P052F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage

P0530.description: General electrical fault on the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit. The ECU uses this signal to enable the compressor and cooling fan; without it the A/C is typically disabled.
P0530.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit

P0531.description: The A/C refrigerant pressure sensor signal is implausible against operating conditions. Reading does not change as expected when the compressor cycles or ambient conditions change.
P0531.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Range/Performance

common_causes: Sensor circuit shorted to ground or open
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0532.description: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage below the lower threshold — open, short to ground, sensor fault, or a refrigerant charge so low that the pressure is genuinely low.
P0532.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0533.description: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage above the upper threshold — short to supply, defective sensor, or a system overcharge/blocked condenser causing genuine high pressure.
P0533.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High

P0534.description: The system detects an abnormally low refrigerant charge. Compressor operation is typically inhibited to prevent damage.
P0534.title: A/C Refrigerant Charge Loss

P0535.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal is missing or out of range. Used to prevent icing of the evaporator core.
P0535.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit

P0536.description: The evaporator temperature sensor used to prevent evaporator icing reports a value within plausible range yet not matching the engine model or cabin conditions.
P0536.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0537.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is below the lower diagnostic threshold. Indicates a short to ground or sensor fault.
P0537.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0538.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is above the upper diagnostic threshold. Typically open circuit or short to power.
P0538.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0539.description: Same as P0536 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0539.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Open in harness or heater element
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P053A.description: The heater on PCV path A - used to prevent ice plugs in the crankcase ventilation hose during cold weather - has an open control circuit. Without it, condensation can freeze and block PCV flow, raising crankcase pressure dangerously.
P053A.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P053B.description: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P053B.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P053C.description: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P053C.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High

P053D.description: The PCV heater on path A is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - hose temperature does not rise as commanded. Heater element aged or contact resistance increased.
P053D.title: PCV Heater A Performance

P053E.description: The crankcase pressure sensor reports a value above the safe upper threshold. Excessive crankcase pressure pushes oil past seals and contaminates the PCV path with mist - causes are clogged PCV system, frozen breather hose, or excessive blow-by from worn rings.
P053E.title: Crankcase Pressure Too High

common_causes: HP pump output low when cold
P053F.description: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation. The pressure target on bank 1 is not reached within the calibrated time window - typical for a high-pressure pump that loses output when cold or a pressure regulator with cold-stickiness.
P053F.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1

P0540.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.
P0540.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0541.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Used on diesel and some petrol engines for cold-start emissions and starting reliability.

The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P0620.description: General electrical fault detected in the alternator/generator control circuit. The ECU regulates field excitation on most modern alternators; a fault here causes charging issues and may set additional battery voltage codes.
P0620.title: Generator Control Circuit

P0621.description: The control circuit for the generator warning lamp output (L terminal) reports a fault.
P0621.title: Generator Lamp L Control Circuit

P0622.description: The control circuit for the generator field terminal (F) reports a fault. The ECM cannot regulate field current as expected.
P0622.title: Generator Field F Control Circuit

P0623.description: Generic generator warning lamp control circuit fault, often used where the lamp terminal designation is not L or where multiple lamps share a single output.
P0623.title: Generator Lamp Control Circuit

P0624.description: The control circuit for the fuel cap warning lamp reports a fault. The ECM cannot drive the indicator that warns of an open or loose fuel cap.
P0624.title: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit

common_causes: Field circuit open or shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0625.description: Voltage on the alternator F terminal (field excitation) is below threshold — open or short to ground in the excitation path.
P0625.title: Generator Field Terminal Circuit Low

P0626.description: The generator field circuit response does not match command. Field current ramps slowly, drifts or fails to reach commanded values during regulation.
P0626.title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Performance

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P0627.description: The ECU detected an open circuit in the fuel pump A control output. With no pump operation the engine cannot run; this code is often paired with no-start and no fuel pressure.
P0627.title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0628.description: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
P0628.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0629.description: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
P0629.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High

P062A.description: The control output to the primary fuel pump A is electrically intact yet response and fuel pressure response do not match - typically a worn pump, a clogged strainer, or a partially shorted PWM driver.
P062A.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Range or Performance

P062B.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "fuel injector control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. P062B.title: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control Performance

The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
P062C.title: Internal Control Module Vehicle Speed Performance

P062D.description: The injector driver stage on bank 1 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.
P062D.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 1

P062E.description: The injector driver stage on bank 2 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.
P062E.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 2

P062F.description: The ECU's EEPROM (persistent calibration storage) reports a check-sum or write error. Calibration values may be corrupted - the ECU runs on safe defaults until repair.
P062F.title: Internal Control Module EEPROM Error

P0630.description: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.
P0630.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM

P0631.description: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.
P0631.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM

P0632.description: The odometer value stored in the ECM/PCM is missing or implausible - typical after a module replacement without odometer programming, or after persistent storage corruption.
P0632.title: Odometer Not Programmed ECM or PCM

P0633.description: The immobiliser system rejects the current key because it is not programmed to this vehicle. Engine start is inhibited.
P0633.title: Immobiliser Key Not Programmed

P0634.description: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition.
P0634.title: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High

P0635.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the power steering control output - typically the line that the ECU uses to request raised idle when steering load is high, or to enable an electric pump.
P0635.title: Power Steering Control Circuit

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0636.description: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0636.title: Power Steering Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0637.description: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0637.title: Power Steering Control Circuit High

P0638.description: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 1 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.
P0638.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 1

P0639.description: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 2 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.
P0639.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 2

common_causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold
P063A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the alternator voltage sense line A - the line over which the regulator measures battery-side voltage to set charging output.
P063A.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A

common_causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold
P063B.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage in plausible range yet not matching the alternator output - high contact resistance or wrong calibration.
P063B.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Range or Performance

common_causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold
P063C.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage below the plausible range.
P063C.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Low

common_causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold
P063D.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage above the plausible range.
P063D.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A High

P063E.description: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.
P063E.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1

P063F.description: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present: the control module has detected this fault condition.
P063F.title: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present

P0640.description: A general circuit fault on the intake air heater control - the ECU cannot drive the grid heater at cold-start.
P0640.title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit

common_causes: Reference wire shorted to ground (one defective sensor pulls the rail down)
Pin pushed back out of connector body
P0641.description: The 5 V reference voltage that the ECU supplies to multiple sensors (TPS, MAP, accelerator pedal, etc.) has dropped out or is open-circuit. Symptoms cascade — many sensor codes appear at once, all related to the same reference rail.
P0641.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Open

common_causes: Sensor or harness shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0642.description: The 5 V reference voltage on the A circuit (used by multiple sensors) is below threshold — short to ground or excessive current draw by a single sensor pulling the rail down.
P0642.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Low

common_causes: Sensor or harness shorted to higher voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0643.description: 5 V reference rail A above threshold — short to a higher voltage source. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0643.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit High

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P0644.description: The serial communication line to the driver display (instrument cluster, MIL/check-engine warning) shows a circuit fault. Driver may not see warning lights as expected.
P0644.title: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit

P0645.description: A general circuit fault on the A/C clutch relay control - the line over which the ECU engages the magnetic clutch to drive the A/C compressor.
P0645.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0646.description: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P0649.description: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.
P0649.title: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit

P064A.description: A general fault is detected on the dedicated fuel pump control module A. Used on PWM-controlled returnless fuel systems to vary pump speed against demand. The module reports an internal performance issue.
P064A.title: Fuel Pump Control Module A

P064B.description: A general fault on the power take-off (PTO) control module - reports internal performance issue or communication trouble. Affects vehicles with auxiliary mechanical drives (cranes, snow ploughs, hydraulic pumps).
P064B.title: PTO Control Module

P064C.description: A general fault is detected on the first glow plug control module - typically a self-diagnosis flag for an internal driver, supply, or watchdog issue.
P064C.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1

common_causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve
P064D.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 1" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
P064D.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1

common_causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P064F.title: Unauthorized Software or Calibration Detected

common_causes: Wiring fault between ECU and cluster
P0650.description: A fault in the wiring or control circuit between the ECU and the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL). The MIL may stay on permanently, fail to light at key-on, or flicker — the OBD-II self-check on the bulb itself failed.
P0650.title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P0651.description: The 5-volt sensor reference rail B is open — the module supplies no voltage on this circuit. Every sensor powered from reference B loses its supply and reads invalid, so the ECU substitutes default values and may limit engine operation. Causes: a broken reference wire, a disconnected connector, or an internal open in the module's voltage regulator for rail B.
P0651.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0653.description: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to supply or above the design voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0656.description: A circuit fault on the fuel level output that the ECU sends to other modules (instrument cluster, range estimator).

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P0657.description: The supply rail that powers a group of actuators (typically injectors, EGR, throttle motor) is open. Multiple downstream actuators stop working.
P0657.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0658.description: Same as P0657 with the supply voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0658.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0659.description: Same as P0657 with the supply voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0659.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit High

P065A.description: A general performance fault in the alternator system - charging output too low or too high under normal load conditions, often caused by a worn brush, a failing regulator, or harness resistance.
P065A.title: Generator System Performance

P065B.description: The PWM control line to the alternator A regulator does not deliver the expected charging response - high contact resistance, regulator drift, or wrong calibration.
P065B.title: Generator A Control Circuit Range or Performance

P065C.description: The alternator A reports a mechanical performance issue - typically a slipping belt, worn pulley clutch, or seizing rotor that causes the output to lag behind speed.
P065C.title: Generator A Mechanical Performance

P065D.description: A circuit fault on the AdBlue malfunction warning lamp output - regulatory in many regions to alert the driver of NOx aftertreatment problems.
P065D.title: Reductant System Malfunction Lamp Control Circuit

common_causes: IMT valve stuck due to carbon
P065E.description: The intake manifold tuning valve (IMT) on bank 1 - which switches the intake runners between long and short paths for torque optimisation - is electrically intact yet does not move as commanded. Carbon build-up, broken linkage, or seized actuator.

common_causes: IMT valve stuck due to carbon
P065F.description: The intake manifold tuning valve (IMT) on bank 2 - which switches the intake runners between long and short paths for torque optimisation - is electrically intact yet does not move as commanded. Carbon build-up, broken linkage, or seized actuator.
P065F.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 2

Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0660.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Open Bank 1
