P0661.description: Same as P0660 with the control line shorted to ground. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
P0661.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0662.description: Same as P0660 with the control line shorted to supply. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
P0662.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 1

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0664.description: Same as P0661 on bank 2. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
P0664.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 2

P0665.description: Same as P0662 on bank 2. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
P0665.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 2

P0667.description: Same as P0666 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine bay environment.

Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P066B.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Control Circuit High

P066C.description: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 2 is shorted to ground or the plug is internally shorted.
P066C.title: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low

Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P066D.description: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 2 is open or shorted to supply - the plug cannot be heated.
P066D.title: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Control Circuit High

P0670.description: The control circuit between the engine controller and the glow plug control module reports a fault. The ECU can no longer reliably command the module that drives the glow plugs, so cold-start pre-heating may not run. On a diesel this causes hard starting, white smoke, and rough running until warm. Causes: open or shorted wiring between ECU and glow plug module, a failed module, or a power/ground fault at the module.
P0670.title: Glow Plug Module Control Circuit

P0671.description: An electrical fault is present in the glow plug circuit for cylinder 1. The glow plug control module cannot drive this plug correctly — open circuit, short, or out-of-range resistance — so cylinder 1 is not pre-heated. On a cold start this causes hard starting, white smoke, and a misfire-like rough run until the engine warms. Causes: a failed glow plug, a broken supply lead to that plug, corrosion at the plug connector, or a faulty module output for cylinder 1.
P0671.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit

P0672.description: An electrical fault is present in the glow plug circuit for cylinder 2. The glow plug control module cannot drive this plug correctly — open circuit, short, or out-of-range resistance — so cylinder 2 is not pre-heated. P0738.description: Same as P0737 with the output shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0738.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0739.description: Same as P0737 with the output shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P0739.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit High

P073A.description: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 5 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-5 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.
P073A.title: Stuck in Gear 5

P073B.description: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 6 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-6 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.
P073B.title: Stuck in Gear 6

P073C.description: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 7 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-7 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.
P073C.title: Stuck in Gear 7

P073D.description: The TCM cannot disengage all gears to neutral - typically a stuck clutch pack or hydraulic pressure issue keeping a gear engaged.
P073D.title: Unable to Engage Neutral

P073E.description: Reverse cannot be engaged when commanded - reverse-band, clutch pack or hydraulic pressure on the reverse circuit has failed.
P073E.title: Unable to Engage Reverse

P073F.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 1 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 1 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-1 circuit.
P073F.title: Unable to Engage Gear 1

P0740.description: A general fault has been detected in the torque converter clutch (TCC) lockup circuit. The TCC mechanically links the engine to the transmission input shaft above a certain speed to eliminate slip and improve fuel economy.
P0740.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Malfunction

common_causes: TCC solenoid stuck or slow to react
Valve body wear (loss of clamping pressure)
P0741.description: When the TCM commands torque converter lockup, the actual slip stays above threshold — the clutch is not engaging. Often signals worn TCC friction material; transmission fluid analysis usually shows debris.
P0741.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P0742.description: The torque converter clutch (TCC) cannot disengage. Symptom is engine stalling when coming to a stop, because the engine is mechanically locked to the transmission output.
P0742.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On

P0743.description: An electrical fault in the torque converter clutch solenoid circuit — open, shorted, or out-of-range driver current. The transmission usually inhibits TCC apply when this code is active.
P0743.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0744.description: The TCC circuit drops in and out — intermittent open or short. Symptoms include erratic shudder at lock-up speeds and intermittent engine stalls when stopping.
P0744.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Intermittent

P0745.description: A general fault on transmission pressure control solenoid A - the solenoid that meters main line pressure for the entire valve body.
P0745.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A

P0746.description: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. It regulates transmission line pressure; faults cause slipping, harsh, or delayed shifts.
P0746.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P0747.description: Pressure control solenoid A appears electrically commanded off but pressure feedback indicates it is stuck on. Line pressure stays high.
P0747.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On

P0748.description: An electrical fault on the pressure control solenoid A circuit - typically open or short to ground or supply.
P0748.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0749.description: Same as P0748 with intermittent or erratic signal.
P0749.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Intermittent

P074A.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 2 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 2 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-2 circuit.
P074A.title: Unable to Engage Gear 2

P074B.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 3 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 3 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-3 circuit.
P074B.title: Unable to Engage Gear 3

P074C.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 4 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 4 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-4 circuit.
P074C.title: Unable to Engage Gear 4

P074D.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 5 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 5 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-5 circuit.
P074D.title: Unable to Engage Gear 5

P074E.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 6 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 6 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-6 circuit.
P074E.title: Unable to Engage Gear 6

P074F.description: The transmission cannot engage gear 7 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 7 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-7 circuit.
P074F.title: Unable to Engage Gear 7

P0750.description: Shift Solenoid "A" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0750.title: Shift Solenoid "A" Malfunction

P0751.description: Shift Solenoid A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0751.title: Shift Solenoid A Performance

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P0752.description: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0752.title: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On

P0753.description: An electrical fault on shift solenoid A - open or short on the control circuit.
P0753.title: Shift Solenoid A Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0754.description: Same as P0753 with intermittent signal.
P0754.title: Shift Solenoid A Intermittent

P0755.description: Shift Solenoid "B" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0755.title: Shift Solenoid "B" Malfunction

P0756.description: Shift Solenoid B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0756.title: Shift Solenoid B Performance

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P0757.description: Shift Solenoid B Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0757.title: Shift Solenoid B Stuck On

P0758.description: Shift Solenoid "B" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0758.title: Shift Solenoid "B" Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0759.description: Same as P0754 on shift solenoid B.
P0759.title: Shift Solenoid B Intermittent

P075A.description: A general fault on shift solenoid G - typically the seventh shift solenoid in transmissions with 7 or more gears.
P075A.title: Shift Solenoid G

common_causes: Solenoid stuck closed by debris in the ATF
Worn valve body bore leaking pressure
P075B.description: Shift solenoid G is electrically intact, but its hydraulic effect is missing — when commanded on, the gear it should engage does not lock up. Either the solenoid is mechanically stuck closed, the valve body bore is worn, or hydraulic pressure does not reach the clutch pack.
P075B.title: Shift Solenoid G Performance/Stuck Off

common_causes: Stuck valve spool in the valve body
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P075C.description: Shift solenoid G remains hydraulically active even when the TCM commands it off. The corresponding clutch or band stays applied, blocking shifts that need it released — typical symptoms are harsh engagement, stuck in a single gear, or refusal to shift cleanly.
P075C.title: Shift Solenoid G Stuck On

common_causes: Damaged wiring at the transmission case connector
P075D.description: General electrical fault on the shift solenoid G control circuit — open coil, short to ground, short to battery voltage, or driver feedback outside the expected range. The TCM disables this solenoid and falls back to limp-home gear logic to protect the transmission.
P075D.title: Shift Solenoid G Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P075E.description: Shift solenoid G shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration on the harness, loose connector, contaminated ATF that occasionally jams the spool, or thermal sensitivity. Difficult to catch with a static check; usually documented by snapshot/freeze-frame data when the fault occurs.
P075E.title: Shift Solenoid G Intermittent

common_causes: Coolant intrusion through a failed transmission cooler
P075F.description: The transmission fluid level monitor reports overfill above the safe maximum. Causes range from incorrect refill at service to coolant intrusion via a failed transmission cooler. Overfilling can cause foaming, accelerated wear and seal damage from raised internal pressure.
P075F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too High

P0760.description: Shift Solenoid "C" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0760.title: Shift Solenoid "C" Malfunction

P0761.description: Shift Solenoid C Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0761.title: Shift Solenoid C Performance

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P0762.description: Shift solenoid C remains hydraulically active when commanded off — the corresponding clutch or band cannot release, locking out shifts that depend on it. The TCM detects the missing release via gear-ratio error or output-shaft slip.
P0762.title: Shift Solenoid C Stuck On

P0763.description: Shift Solenoid "C" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0763.title: Shift Solenoid "C" Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0764.description: Shift solenoid C shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration, loose connector, ATF contamination or thermal sensitivity. Hard to reproduce on a static bench check.
P0764.title: Shift Solenoid C Intermittent

P0765.description: Shift Solenoid "D" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0765.title: Shift Solenoid "D" Malfunction

P0766.description: Shift Solenoid D Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0766.title: Shift Solenoid D Performance

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P0767.description: Shift solenoid D remains hydraulically active when commanded off — corresponding clutch or band cannot release. The TCM detects the missing release via gear-ratio error.
P0767.title: Shift Solenoid D Stuck On

P0768.description: Shift Solenoid "D" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0768.title: Shift Solenoid "D" Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0769.description: Shift solenoid D shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts.
P0769.title: Shift Solenoid D Intermittent

P076A.description: General fault on shift solenoid H — used in 8/9/10-speed transmissions where multiple shift solenoids manage the larger gear matrix. The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly without yet being able to attribute it to a specific failure mode.
P076A.title: Shift Solenoid H

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P076B.description: Shift solenoid H is electrically intact but does not engage hydraulically when commanded — corresponding clutch or band does not lock up.
P076B.title: Shift Solenoid H Performance/Stuck Off

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P076C.description: Shift solenoid H remains hydraulically active when commanded off — corresponding clutch or band cannot release, blocking dependent shifts.
P076C.title: Shift Solenoid H Stuck On

common_causes: Damaged wiring at the transmission connector
P076D.description: General electrical fault on the shift solenoid H control circuit — open coil, short to ground or battery, driver feedback outside range.
P076D.title: Shift Solenoid H Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P076E.description: Shift solenoid H shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts.
P076E.title: Shift Solenoid H Intermittent

common_causes: Wrong shift solenoid pattern engaging the wrong gear
P076F.description: While in 7th gear, the ratio measured between input shaft speed and output shaft speed does not match the calibrated value for that gear. Either a clutch or band is slipping, the wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data is wrong.
P076F.title: Gear 7 Incorrect Ratio

P0770.description: General fault on shift solenoid E. The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly that has not yet been pinned to a specific failure mode.
P0770.title: Shift Solenoid E

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P0771.description: Shift solenoid E is electrically intact but does not engage hydraulically — associated clutch or band does not lock up.
P0771.title: Shift Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play
P0772.description: Shift solenoid E remains hydraulically active when commanded off — associated clutch or band cannot release, blocking dependent shifts.
P0772.title: Shift Solenoid E Stuck On

P0773.description: Shift Solenoid "E" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
P0773.title: Shift Solenoid "E" Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0774.description: Shift solenoid E shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration, loose connector or ATF contamination.
P0774.title: Shift Solenoid E Intermittent

P0775.description: Generic fault on pressure control solenoid B circuit. Either electrical or response fault depending on manufacturer.
P0775.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B

P0776.description: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. It regulates transmission line pressure; faults cause slipping, harsh, or delayed shifts.
P0776.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance

common_causes: Contaminated ATF clogging the pressure control valve
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P0777.description: Pressure control solenoid B does not release line pressure when commanded — output pressure remains at maximum, leading to harsh shifts and elevated stress on the clutch packs and seals.
P0777.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On

common_causes: Damaged wiring at the transmission case connector
P0778.description: General electrical fault on the pressure control solenoid B circuit — open coil, short to ground or battery, or driver feedback outside the expected range.
P0778.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0779.description: Pressure control solenoid B shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration, loose connector, or contaminated ATF that occasionally restricts the regulator port.
P0779.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Intermittent

P077A.description: The output shaft speed sensor uses a quadrature output (two channels phase-shifted by 90°) so the TCM can determine direction of rotation. The direction channel is missing — TCM cannot tell whether the vehicle is rolling forward or backward, blocking neutral-idle and rollback-protection strategies.
P077A.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit - Loss of Direction Signal

P077B.description: The TCM reads a direction from the output shaft speed sensor that contradicts the commanded gear — for example reverse direction while drive is engaged, or forward direction while reverse is engaged. Either the sensor wiring is swapped, the sensor is wrong, or the gear actually engaged is not the one commanded.
P077B.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit - Direction Error

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P077C.description: Output shaft speed sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply. TCM disables vehicle-speed dependent shift logic and may force limp-home.
P077C.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P077D.description: Output shaft speed sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.
P077D.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High

P077E.description: Modern transmissions can have two or more ATF temperature sensors (sump, cooler return, valve body). After a long key-off soak they should all read approximately the same ambient. The TCM detects an implausible spread between sensors — one of them drifts or is wired wrong.
P077E.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation

P077F.description: Some transmissions provide a second reverse ratio (typically a slower crawler reverse for trailer manoeuvring or hill descent). The TCM detects that the input/output ratio in this gear does not match its calibrated value — slipping clutch or wrong gear actually engaged.
P077F.title: Reverse 2 Incorrect Ratio

P0780.description: The TCM detects that a commanded shift between gears did not occur within the expected time and quality window. Slip rates or speed ratios remain implausible during shift.
P0780.title: Shift Malfunction

P0781.description: The TCM detects a fault during the 1-to-2 upshift. The actual gear ratio after the shift command does not match the expected ratio for second gear.
P0781.title: 1-2 Shift Malfunction

P0782.description: The TCM detects a fault during the 2-to-3 upshift. Gear ratio after shift command does not match third gear expected ratio.
P0782.title: 2-3 Shift Malfunction

P0783.description: The TCM detects a fault during the 3-to-4 upshift, where gear ratio after the shift does not match fourth gear expected value.
P0783.title: 3-4 Shift Malfunction

P0784.description: The TCM detects a fault during the 4-to-5 upshift on transmissions equipped with five or more forward gears.
P0784.title: 4-5 Shift Malfunction

P0785.description: General fault on shift timing solenoid A — controls the rate at which a shift event takes place (smooth ramp vs. quick snap). The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly that has not yet been pinned to a specific failure mode.
P0785.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A

common_causes: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0786.description: Shift timing solenoid A is electrically intact, but the actual shift time does not match the model — shifts too fast (harsh) or too slow (slipping under load). Often aged solenoid with weakened force or contaminated ATF restricting the regulating port.
P0786.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Range/Performance

P0787.description: Shift timing solenoid A control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.
P0787.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Low

common_causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
P0788.description: Shift timing solenoid A control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return.
P0788.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0789.description: Shift timing solenoid A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or thermal sensitivity.
P0789.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Intermittent

P078A.description: General fault on shift timing solenoid B — second timing solenoid for shift events that need a different ramp profile (typically downshifts vs. upshifts, or specific gear pairs).
P078A.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P078B.description: Shift timing solenoid B is electrically intact, but actual shift timing does not match the model — same failure modes as solenoid A (aged, dirty ATF), applied to the second timing channel.
P078B.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Range/Performance

P078C.description: Shift timing solenoid B control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground.
P078C.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Low

common_causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
P078D.description: Shift timing solenoid B control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil.
P078D.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P078E.description: Shift timing solenoid B signal jumps or drops out.
P078E.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Intermittent

P078F.description: General electrical fault on the third transmission mode select switch input C — used for additional drive modes (Sport, Snow, Tow/Haul, Eco) on transmissions that offer more than two operator-selectable shift maps. Without a valid input the TCM falls back to the default mode.
P078F.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit

P0790.description: General electrical fault on the Normal/Performance shift-pattern selector switch — lets the driver toggle between a comfort-oriented and a sport-oriented shift map. Without a valid input the TCM defaults to the Normal map.
P0790.title: Normal/Performance Switch Circuit

P0791.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault on the intermediate shaft speed sensor A circuit. Used to compute shift slip and torque converter behavior.
P0791.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Aged Hall element with reduced amplitude
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0792.description: The intermediate shaft speed sensor (between input and output, used in CVT and dual-clutch boxes for slip detection between gear elements) is electrically intact, but its readings drift away from the model. The TCM cannot reliably detect slip in this stage.
P0792.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

P0793.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A is connected and powered, but no rotation pulses arrive while the transmission is in motion. Either the sensor reluctor wheel is damaged, the sensor air gap is wrong, or the element has failed open.
P0793.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0794.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or oil mist on the sensor tip.
P0794.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

P0795.description: General fault on pressure control solenoid C — third pressure regulator in transmissions with multiple independently regulated hydraulic circuits (line pressure, clutch C, torque converter clutch). The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly that has not yet been pinned to a specific failure mode.
P0795.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C

P0796.description: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. It regulates transmission line pressure; faults cause slipping, harsh, or delayed shifts.
P0796.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P0797.description: The TCM detects that pressure control solenoid C remains energized hydraulically despite commanded de-energization. Line pressure or shift quality deviates from target.
P0797.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Stuck On

P0798.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault in the pressure control solenoid C circuit, such as open winding, short to ground or short to power.
P0798.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Electrical

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0799.description: Pressure control solenoid C shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts.
P0799.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Intermittent

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element A
Low hydraulic pressure to element A
P079A.description: Friction element A (the first clutch or band in the gear matrix) shows measurable slip while it should be fully engaged. Detected by comparing input/output speed sensors against the commanded gear ratio. Slip means the element cannot transmit full torque — risk of glazing the friction surfaces.
P079A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element B
P079B.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element B (the second clutch or band).
P079B.title: Transmission Friction Element B Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element C
P079C.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element C (third clutch or band).
P079C.title: Transmission Friction Element C Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element D
P079D.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element D (fourth clutch or band).
P079D.title: Transmission Friction Element D Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element E
P079E.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element E (fifth clutch or band, used in 8/9/10-speed transmissions).
P079E.title: Transmission Friction Element E Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element F
P079F.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element F (sixth clutch or band, used in 8/9/10-speed transmissions).
P079F.title: Transmission Friction Element F Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element G
P07A0.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element G (seventh clutch or band, used in 9/10-speed transmissions).
P07A0.title: Transmission Friction Element G Slip Detected

common_causes: Worn friction discs in element H
P07A1.description: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element H (eighth clutch or band, in 10-speed transmissions).
P07A1.title: Transmission Friction Element H Slip Detected

P07A2.description: Friction element A does not lock up when commanded — its hydraulic circuit cannot bring the clutch pack into full engagement. Either the apply piston is stuck, the seal is leaking past the piston, or the supplying pressure regulator is failing.
P07A2.title: Transmission Friction Element A Performance/Stuck Off

P07A3.title: Transmission Friction Element A Stuck On

P07B2.description: Park position sensor/switch A — confirms that the gear selector lever is in Park, used by shift-by-wire systems and key-interlock logic — is open. The TCM cannot confirm Park engagement, blocking key removal and engine restart logic.
P07B2.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P07B3.description: Park position sensor/switch A reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07B3.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P07B4.description: Park position sensor/switch A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07B4.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High

P07B5.description: Sensor A is electrically intact but its low-end value drifts — for example a value below the calibrated Park threshold while the lever is mechanically out of Park. The TCM cannot fully trust the Park reading.
P07B5.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance/Low

P07B6.description: Sensor A is electrically intact but the high-end value drifts — for example a value above the calibrated non-Park range while the lever actually is in Park.
P07B6.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P07B7.description: Park position sensor A signal jumps or drops out — typically a worn switch with contact bounce or a loose connector at the shift lever module.
P07B7.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P07B8.description: Park position sensor/switch B is the redundant/secondary park-confirmation sensor — used in shift-by-wire systems for safety, so a single sensor failure cannot strand the vehicle in Park or hide a non-Park condition. With B open the TCM falls back to sensor A only.
P07B8.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit/Open

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P07B9.description: Park sensor/switch B reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07B9.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low

Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07BA.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High

P07BB.description: Sensor B low-end value drifts away from the calibrated Park threshold.
P07BB.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance/Low

P07BC.description: Sensor B high-end value drifts above the calibrated non-Park range.
P07BC.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance High

P07BD.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P07BE.description: The two redundant park position sensors A and B disagree — one reports Park, the other does not. Until the discrepancy is cleared the TCM cannot trust either reading and falls back to a safe state (typically blocking key removal and engine restart).
P07BE.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A/B Correlation

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07CA.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit High

P07CB.description: The transmission fluid thermostat (similar in function to a coolant thermostat — opens at a calibrated temperature to route ATF through the cooler) does not regulate temperature within the expected band. Either stuck open (ATF stays cold, friction modifier ineffective) or stuck closed (ATF overheats, oxidising the fluid).
P07CB.title: Transmission Fluid Thermostat Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P07CC.description: Transmission mode switch C input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07CC.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit Low

Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07CD.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit High

P07CF.description: Mode switch D input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P07D5.description: Mode switch F input reads stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P07D6.description: Mode switch F input reads stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

P07D7.description: The transmission has entered 8th gear but cannot leave it on command — typically a stuck shift solenoid or a stuck-on friction element holding the 8th-gear pattern locked. The TCM forces limp-home mode if upshift/downshift attempts fail repeatedly.
P07D7.title: Stuck in Gear 8

P07D8.description: The TCM commands a shift to 8th gear but the gear-ratio measurement does not confirm engagement — friction element does not lock up, slipping clutch, or shift solenoid does not respond. Falls back to the previously engaged gear.
P07D8.title: Unable To Engage Gear 8

P07D9.description: While in 8th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value — slipping clutch, wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data wrong.
P07D9.title: Gear 8 Incorrect Ratio

P07DA.description: General fault detected during the 6-to-7 upshift event — slipping during the shift, gear-ratio overshoot, or shift completion timeout. Often a worn friction element on the 7th-gear side or a slow shift solenoid.
P07DA.title: 6-7 Shift

P07DB.description: General fault detected during the 7-to-8 upshift event.
P07DB.title: 7-8 Shift

P07DC.description: Starting from 1st gear, the TCM commanded a specific upshift but the resulting gear ratio matches a different gear. Wrong shift solenoid pattern actually engaged, or a stuck solenoid blocked the intended pattern.
P07DC.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 1

P07DD.description: Same condition as incorrect shift from gear 1, applied to shifts originating in 2nd gear.
P07DD.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 2

P07DE.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 3rd gear.
P07DE.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 3

P07DF.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 4th gear.
P07DF.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 4

P07E0.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 5th gear.
P07E0.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 5

P07E1.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 6th gear.
P07E1.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 6

P07E2.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 7th gear.
P07E2.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 7

P07E3.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 8th gear.
P07E3.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 8

common_causes: Park pawl jammed against tooth (rock vehicle to release)
P07E4.description: The TCM commands the park pawl to engage but the position sensors do not confirm engagement — typical for shift-by-wire systems where the park actuator (motor or solenoid driving the pawl) is faulty, the cable is broken, or the pawl is jammed against a tooth and cannot drop in.
P07E4.title: Unable to Engage Park

P07E5.description: TCM commands engagement of Drive but the input/output speed relationship does not match — friction element does not lock up, or the shift solenoid pattern for Drive cannot be commanded. Vehicle remains stuck in Park or Neutral.
P07E5.title: Unable to Engage Drive

P07E6.description: The vehicle cannot leave Park even though the operator has commanded a different range. Park pawl jammed, park actuator failed, or shift-by-wire input not received by TCM.
P07E6.title: Stuck in Park

P07E7.description: The vehicle cannot leave Drive — typically a stuck shift mechanism, a stuck-on friction element, or a TCM that cannot command the shift to Park or Neutral.
P07E7.title: Stuck in Drive

common_causes: Open wire to the range actuator
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P07E8.description: The transmission range control A circuit (used in shift-by-wire to drive the shift actuator that physically positions the manual valve in the valve body) is open. The TCM cannot move the manual valve into the commanded range, blocking shifts between P/R/N/D.
P07E8.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit/Open

P07E9.description: Range control A circuit is electrically intact, but the actuator response does not match the model — for example position feedback that does not move when commanded, or moves slower than expected. Often a sticking actuator or aged motor.
P07E9.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P07EA.description: Range control A circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07EA.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low

common_causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P07EB.description: Range control A circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07EB.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit High

P07EC.description: General electrical fault on the multi-function transmission range select circuit — used on shift-by-wire systems with rotary or push-button selectors that encode P/R/N/D as a multi-bit pattern. With the input invalid the TCM cannot decode the operator request.
P07EC.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit

P07ED.description: The multi-function select circuit reports a value that does not change despite operator activity — the rotary encoder is stuck or a push-button is mechanically locked. The TCM ignores further requests until the input becomes plausible.
P07ED.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P07EE.description: The multi-function select circuit produces values that do not match any valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted simultaneously, or values outside the calibrated range.
P07EE.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P07EF.description: Multi-function select circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07EF.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P07F0.description: Multi-function select circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or pegged at maximum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P07F0.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High

P07F1.description: General electrical fault on input/turbine speed sensor C — third input speed sensor in heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions.
P07F1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
P07F2.description: General fault on the communication line between the TCM and a separate transmission range control module (used on systems where the rotary/push-button selector lives in its own intelligent module that talks to the TCM via CAN or LIN).
P07F2.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P07F3.description: Range control module communication line reads stuck low — bus shorted to ground or one node held the line low continuously.
P07F3.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec
P07F4.description: Range control module communication line reads stuck high — bus shorted to battery voltage or open at the bus terminator.
P07F4.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High

P07F5.description: The range control module reports its supply voltage below the operating threshold — vehicle battery low, charging system underperforming, or supply line resistance excessive. The module may stop responding until voltage recovers.
P07F5.title: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low

P07F6.description: While in 9th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value — slipping clutch, wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data wrong.
P07F6.title: Gear 9 Incorrect Ratio

P07F7.description: While in 10th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value.
P07F7.title: Gear 10 Incorrect Ratio

P07F8.description: Same condition as stuck in 8th gear, applied to 9th.
P07F8.title: Stuck in Gear 9

P07F9.description: Same condition as unable to engage 8th gear, applied to 9th.
P07F9.title: Unable to Engage Gear 9

P07FA.description: Same condition as incorrect shift from 8th, applied to 9th.
P07FA.title: Incorrect Shift From Gear 9

P07FB.description: Same condition as stuck in 8th, applied to 10th.
P07FB.title: Stuck in Gear 10

P07FC.description: Same condition as unable to engage 8th, applied to 10th.
P07FC.title: Unable to Engage Gear 10

P07FD.description: Same condition as incorrect shift from 8th, applied to 10th.
P07FD.title: Incorrect Shift From Gear 10

P07FE.description: The TCM detects that the transmission is stuck in some gear but cannot identify which one — typically because multiple input/output ratio cross-checks fail simultaneously, or an early-detection diagnostic fires before the specific-gear detection runs.
P07FE.title: Stuck In Gear - Not Specified

P07FF.description: During the cold-start phase the transmission does not behave to specification — typically very slow shifts, missed shifts or harsh engagement at low ATF temperature. Common causes are degraded ATF (lost cold-flow viscosity), a stuck thermostat or aged solenoid drivers.
P07FF.title: Cold Start Transmission Performance

common_causes: Internal fault in transfer case module — read its DTCs
P0800.description: The transfer case control module has requested the ECM/PCM to illuminate the MIL because of a fault on its side that is emissions- or driveline-relevant. The original fault is in the transfer case module itself.
P0800.title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)

P0801.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault in the reverse inhibit solenoid circuit, which prevents engagement of reverse at high vehicle speeds.
P0801.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor
P0802.description: The dedicated MIL request line from the TCM to the ECM (used in older systems where modules used a hard wire to ask for the MIL instead of CAN messaging) is open. The ECM cannot honour TCM-side MIL requests.
P0802.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open

P0803.description: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift solenoid control circuit — used on manual-transmission performance vehicles to force a skip from 1st straight to 4th under low-load cruise (CAFE fuel-economy feature). With the input invalid the lockout cannot be applied.
P0803.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit

P0804.description: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift indicator lamp control circuit — the dashboard light that prompts the driver to skip from 1st straight to 4th. With the input invalid the lamp cannot be illuminated.
P0804.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit

P0805.description: General electrical fault on the clutch position sensor A circuit — used in dual-clutch and automated-manual transmissions to monitor clutch fork or release-bearing position. Without a valid signal the TCM cannot close the loop on clutch engagement.
P0805.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P0806.description: Clutch position sensor A is electrically intact, but its readings drift away from the model — for example the position does not move when the actuator is commanded, or the offset shifts after a thermal cycle. Often a misadjusted sensor mount.
P0806.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P0807.description: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference voltage.
P0807.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low

common_causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source
P0808.description: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.
P0808.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High

common_causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration
P0809.description: Clutch position sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or oil/heat exposure near the bell housing.
P0809.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent

common_causes: Learn cycle not performed after service
P080A.description: After a clutch replacement or sensor replacement the TCM has not run a successful clutch-position learn cycle. Without learned end-stops the TCM cannot accurately command engagement points, leading to slipping or harsh take-up. A scan-tool guided learn procedure must be performed.
P080A.title: Clutch Position Not Learned

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
P080B.description: Skip-shift solenoid is electrically intact, but the lockout effect does not match commands — solenoid sticks or coil aged, gearbox interlock cannot be applied or released within the expected time.
P080B.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P080C.description: Skip-shift solenoid control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P080C.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low

common_causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P080D.description: Skip-shift solenoid control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
P080D.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High

P0810.description: On automated manual or dual-clutch transmissions, the actual clutch actuator position deviates from commanded position beyond tolerance. Position sensor and actuator do not agree on closed-loop test.
P0810.title: Clutch Position Control Error

common_causes: Low clamp force from aged actuator
P0811.description: The TCM detects more slip across clutch A (the first clutch in dual-clutch boxes, or the launch clutch in automated-manual systems) than the calibration allows. Heat builds up rapidly — risk of glazing the friction discs or warping the pressure plate.
P0811.title: Excessive Clutch A Slippage

common_causes: Open or shorted reverse input wire
P0812.description: General electrical fault on the reverse-engagement input — the signal that tells the TCM (and other modules — backup lights, parking sensors) that the gear lever is in Reverse. With the input invalid backup lights and rear sensors do not activate.
P0812.title: Reverse Input Circuit

P0813.description: General electrical fault on the reverse-output circuit — the line that drives backup lights, reverse alarm or transfer-case reverse signal. With the output broken these consumers cannot be activated.

common_causes: Sulphur poisoning from high-sulphur fuel — desulphation regeneration not running
Thermal aging of washcoat after high-temperature exposure
P2000.description: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 1 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.
P2000.title: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)

P2001.description: The lean NOx trap (LNT) on bank 2 is no longer storing or releasing NOx within the required efficiency window. Detected by the downstream NOx sensor or model-based monitor — typically caused by sulphur poisoning, thermal aging, or a failed regeneration strategy.
P2001.title: NOx Adsorber Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)

common_causes: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
Filter substrate cracked or melted from runaway regeneration
P2002.description: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1): the control module has detected this fault condition.
P2002.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)

common_causes: DPF heavily loaded — repeated short trips prevent regeneration
P2003.description: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2): the control module has detected this fault condition.
P2003.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)

common_causes: IMRC actuator or vacuum motor failed
P2004.description: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.
P2004.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)

common_causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2005.description: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flap on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. The IMRC swirls or tumbles intake charge at low rpm by closing one runner per cylinder; when stuck open, low-end torque drops and the engine may misfire on cold starts.
P2005.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 2)

common_causes: Actuator stuck or vacuum line collapsed
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2006.description: The IMRC flap on bank 1 is stuck in the closed position and cannot open at higher rpm. Top-end power suffers because the runner is restricted, and the engine may breathe poorly above mid-range.
P2006.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)

common_causes: Carbon deposits seize flap closed on bank 2
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
P2007.description: Bank 2 counterpart to P2006. The IMRC flap on bank 2 cannot return to the open position and chokes intake flow at higher rpm.
P2007.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 2)

common_causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
P2008.description: The ECU detects an open circuit on the IMRC solenoid for bank 1. No control current flows when the runner is commanded to switch, leaving the flap in its default position.
P2008.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Open (Bank 1)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2009.description: The IMRC solenoid drive line for bank 1 reads below the lower threshold — short to ground or a failed driver stage. The runner cannot be switched on demand.
P2009.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)

common_causes: Actuator weak or vacuum supply low
Linkage worn — play between actuator and flap
P200A.description: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 1 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.
P200A.title: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 1)

P200B.description: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) on bank 2 reports that flap movement does not match the commanded position within the allowed time window — either too slow, too short a stroke, or position feedback off-target.
P200B.title: Intake Manifold Runner Performance (Bank 2)

common_causes: Excessive soot load triggers runaway regeneration
DPF temperature sensor reading drifts high
P200C.description: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 1 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.
P200C.title: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 1)

P200D.description: A temperature sensor at the diesel particulate filter (DPF) on bank 2 has exceeded the safe limit — typically during a runaway regeneration. Continued operation can melt or crack the substrate.
P200D.title: Particulate Filter Over Temperature (Bank 2)

common_causes: Persistent misfire dumps unburned fuel into the cat
Sustained rich mixture from leaking injector or fuel pressure regulator
P200E.description: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 1 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.
P200E.title: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 1)

P200F.description: A temperature sensor in the exhaust catalyst on bank 2 reports a value above the safe operating limit. Sustained over-temperature can sinter the precious-metal washcoat and destroy conversion efficiency.
P200F.title: Catalyst System Over Temperature (Bank 2)

common_causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2010.description: Drive voltage at the IMRC solenoid on bank 1 is above the upper limit — short to supply or an open ground side. The solenoid is energised constantly or the driver protection trips.
P2010.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)

common_causes: Open wiring or chafed conductor in IMRC harness
P2011.description: The IMRC actuator drive circuit on bank 2 is open or has lost continuity — control module no longer detects a closing path through the actuator winding.
P2011.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit/Open (Bank 2)

common_causes: Short to ground in driver line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2012.description: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads below the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to ground or a stuck-low driver inside the control module.
P2012.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Low (Bank 2)

common_causes: Short to B+ in driver line
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
P2013.description: The IMRC actuator drive line on bank 2 reads above the expected voltage threshold — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground side.
P2013.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit High (Bank 2)

P2014.description: The position feedback signal of the IMRC flap on bank 1 is missing or implausible. Without feedback, the ECU cannot verify that the commanded runner position has been reached.
P2014.title: Intake Manifold Runner Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)

common_causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
