P3466.description: The engine control module has detected an open hydraulic circuit in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 1. The system uses pressurized engine oil routed through dedicated lifters and oil control valves to collapse valves; an open circuit indicates loss of oil flow or a failed pressure switch.
P3466.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Open

common_causes: Incorrect oil viscosity or aged oil
Internal oil leak in deactivation circuit
P3467.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit used for cylinder deactivation. Oil pressure response or timing is outside the expected window during deactivation events, often caused by viscosity issues, internal leaks or worn lifters.
P3467.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Performance

P3468.description: The engine control module has detected low oil pressure in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit responsible for cylinder deactivation. Below threshold pressure the lifters cannot collapse and the system disables further deactivation requests on bank 1.
P3468.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 Low

P3469.description: The engine control module has detected an excessively high oil pressure or stuck-on signal in the bank 1 hydraulic circuit for cylinder deactivation. Either a stuck oil control valve, a blocked relief path, or a shorted pressure switch is reporting permanently high pressure.
P3469.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 1 High

common_causes: Oil passage blocked or sludge buildup
P3470.description: The engine control module has detected an open hydraulic circuit in the cylinder deactivation system on bank 2. Loss of oil flow, a failed oil pressure switch or a disconnected oil control valve prevents the system from deactivating cylinders on bank 2.

common_causes: Incorrect oil viscosity or aged oil
Internal oil leak in deactivation circuit
P3471.description: The engine control module has detected a performance fault in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit used for cylinder deactivation. P3471.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Performance

P3472.description: The engine control module has detected low oil pressure in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit responsible for cylinder deactivation. Below the calibrated threshold the switching lifters cannot collapse and cylinder deactivation on bank 2 is disabled until pressure recovers.
P3472.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 Low

P3473.description: The engine control module has detected a fault in the cylinder 9 deactivation system. Found on V10/V12 engines with cylinder deactivation — cylinder 9 cannot reliably switch state.

P3474.description: The engine control module has detected an excessively high oil pressure or stuck-on signal in the bank 2 hydraulic circuit for cylinder deactivation. A stuck oil control valve, a blocked relief path or a shorted pressure switch is reporting permanently high pressure on bank 2.
P3474.title: Cylinder Deactivation Hydraulic Circuit Bank 2 High

P3475.description: The engine control module has detected an electrical fault in the cylinder deactivation oil pressure switch circuit on bank 1. U0001.description: A general fault on the high-speed CAN bus has been detected. This bus typically connects powertrain modules (ECM, TCM, ABS) at 500 kbit/s and a fault disables communication between them, often triggering multiple secondary DTCs in other modules.
U0001.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus

common_causes: Corrosion or poor contact in CAN connectors
U0002.description: The high-speed CAN bus is functional but performance is degraded — frame errors, bit errors or excessive bus load have been detected. Communication may be intermittent rather than completely lost, leading to sporadic warning lamps.
U0002.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus Performance

common_causes: CAN-High wire broken or pin pushed back
Harness damage after repair or accident
U0003.description: The CAN-High line of the high-speed bus is open. Without the differential pair, the controller cannot decode any traffic and reports loss of all participating modules at once. Often follows a wiring repair, accident damage, or a corroded connector pin.
U0003.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Open

common_causes: Internal transceiver failure on a node
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0004.description: The CAN-High signal stays below its valid voltage window. Common cause is a short to ground on the CAN-H wire or a transceiver that pulls the line down. The bus stops working until the offending node is isolated.
U0004.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Low

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0005.description: The CAN-High line is held above its valid voltage range, usually because of a short to battery voltage. Bus communication collapses for every connected module.
U0005.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) High

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0006.description: The CAN-Low wire of the high-speed bus is open. The differential signal can no longer be evaluated correctly, so all bus participants report communication loss simultaneously.
U0006.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Open

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0007.description: The CAN-Low line is shorted to ground or held below its valid recessive level. The differential pair cannot transmit data and the bus is effectively dead.
U0007.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Low

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0008.description: The CAN-Low signal is held above its valid range, typically because of a short to battery voltage on the CAN-L wire. Bus communication is lost for every node sharing this segment.
U0008.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) High

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0009.description: CAN-High and CAN-Low are shorted together. The differential signal collapses to zero and the bus controller can no longer separate dominant from recessive bits, so all communication stops.
U0009.title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Shorted to Bus (+)

common_causes: MS-CAN line shorted to supply or ground

U0010.description: A fault on the medium-speed CAN bus has been detected. This bus (typically 125 kbit/s) connects body and comfort modules — BCM, climate, doors, infotainment. A failure usually disables comfort functions but leaves the powertrain operational.

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

U0100.description: The ECM/PCM "A" has stopped transmitting on the vehicle data bus, so other control units no longer receive its messages. As this is the engine controller itself, the engine usually will not start or run while the message is missing. Typical causes are loss of power or ground at the module, an open or shorted CAN/LIN bus wire, a connector fault, or an internal module failure.
U0100.title: Lost Communication with ECM/PCM "A"

U0296.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with AC/DC converter (on-board charger) module A. Charging from AC sources cannot be controlled and the high-voltage battery does not refill via this path.

U029B.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with drive motor control module C. Torque commands for this EV/hybrid traction motor cannot be coordinated, forcing the powertrain into a degraded mode.

U029C.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with drive motor control module D. Torque commands for this EV/hybrid traction motor cannot be coordinated, forcing the powertrain into a degraded mode.

U029D.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with NOx sensor A (smart sensor with own ECU). The SCR catalyst control loop loses its actual NOx feedback and may switch to substitute values.

U029E.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with NOx sensor B (smart sensor with own ECU). The SCR catalyst control loop loses its actual NOx feedback and may switch to substitute values.

U029F.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the EVAP leak detection module. Tank-pressure / vacuum diagnostics for fuel-vapour leaks cannot be commanded.

U02A1.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with NOx sensor C (smart sensor with own ECU). The SCR catalyst control loop loses its actual NOx feedback and may switch to substitute values.

U02A2.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the reductant (DEF/AdBlue) quality sensor module. The SCR system cannot verify urea concentration; emissions countermeasures may activate.
U02A2.title: Lost Communication With Reductant Quality Module

U02A3.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the particulate matter (PM) sensor (smart sensor with own ECU). DPF post-cat soot monitoring loses its primary feedback signal.
U02A3.title: Lost Communication With Particulate Matter Sensor

U02A4.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor downstream of the SCR. Detection of urea over-dosing is impaired.
U02A4.title: Lost Communication With NH3 Sensor

U02A5.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the reductant heater module. AdBlue lines and tank can no longer be thawed at low temperatures, blocking SCR operation in winter.
U02A5.title: Lost Communication With Reductant Heater Control Module

U02A6.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the safety integration module that arbitrates between ADAS, restraint, brake and steering systems. Cross-system safety functions may be inhibited.
U02A6.title: Lost Communication With Safety Integration Control Module

U02A7.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with engine sound control unit 1. Active sound design (interior synthetic engine sound or exterior pedestrian alert) for this channel stops.
U02A7.title: Lost Communication With Engine Sound Control 1

U02A8.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with engine sound control unit 2. Active sound design (interior synthetic engine sound or exterior pedestrian alert) for this channel stops.
U02A8.title: Lost Communication With Engine Sound Control 2

U02A9.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with charge air cooler (intercooler) coolant pump A. Intake-charge cooling on indirect intercooler systems cannot be controlled, raising knock risk and reducing power.

U02AA.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the hybrid engine disconnect clutch actuator. Switching between EV-only and combustion drive can no longer be commanded smoothly.

U02AB.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the vehicle thermal management module. Coordination of engine, battery and cabin cooling/heating loops is lost; sub-modules fall back to local control.
U02AB.title: Lost Communication With Vehicle Thermal Management Control Module

U02AC.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with boost control module A (electric wastegate or VTG actuator). Boost pressure cannot be commanded; the engine reverts to a low-power fallback.
U02AC.title: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A

U02AD.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with boost control module B (electric wastegate or VTG actuator). Boost pressure cannot be commanded; the engine reverts to a low-power fallback.
U02AD.title: Lost Communication With Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B

U02AE.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the high-voltage battery coolant pump. Active battery cooling cannot be regulated; charging/discharging power may be limited to protect the cells.
U02AE.title: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Battery Coolant Pump

U02AF.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the turbocharger turbine inlet valve position sensor. Position feedback for variable inlet geometry on twin-scroll/sequential turbo systems is missing.
U02AF.title: Lost Communication With Turbocharger Turbine Inlet Valve Position Sensor

U02B0.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the boost control B position sensor. Closed-loop control of the wastegate/VTG actuator on this turbo loses its actual feedback signal.

U02B1.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with comfort and convenience display A (typically a rear-seat or passenger screen for climate, audio, ambient lighting). It freezes or goes blank.

U02B2.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with comfort and convenience display B (typically a rear-seat or passenger screen for climate, audio, ambient lighting). It freezes or goes blank.
U02B2.title: Lost Communication With Comfort and Convenience Display B

U02B3.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the driver monitoring system (DMS) module. Eye/head-pose tracking for drowsiness, distraction and hands-on detection is unavailable, and dependent ADAS handover features may be inhibited.
U02B3.title: Lost Communication With Driver Monitoring System Module

U02B4.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with front radar module A. Adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking and forward collision warning lose their primary range/closing-speed input.
U02B4.title: Lost Communication With Front Radar Module A

U02B5.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with front radar module B. Adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking and forward collision warning lose their primary range/closing-speed input.
U02B5.title: Lost Communication With Front Radar Module B

U02B6.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with rear radar module A. Blind-spot warning, lane-change assist and rear cross-traffic alert dependent on this sensor are inhibited.

U02B7.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with rear radar module B. Blind-spot warning, lane-change assist and rear cross-traffic alert dependent on this sensor are inhibited.
U02B7.title: Lost Communication With Rear Radar Module B

U02B8.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with rear radar module C. Blind-spot warning, lane-change assist and rear cross-traffic alert dependent on this sensor are inhibited.

U02B9.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with rear radar module D. Blind-spot warning, lane-change assist and rear cross-traffic alert dependent on this sensor are inhibited.
U02B9.title: Lost Communication With Rear Radar Module D

U02BA.title: Lost Communication With Hybrid/EV Electronics Coolant Pump B

U02BB.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with the EVAP purge pump (used on systems with electric purging instead of intake-vacuum). Vapour purge from the carbon canister cannot be commanded.

Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U05C0.description: A receiving module detected implausible data from interior lighting control module B. Ambient lighting zone, reading lamp or door courtesy light commands fail plausibility checks and are rejected.
U05C0.title: Invalid Data Received From Interior Lighting Control Module B

common_causes: Module internal fault or sensor input drift
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U05C1.description: A receiving module detected implausible data from active radiator air flow control module A. Active grille shutter or fan staging values fail plausibility checks and are rejected.
U05C1.title: Invalid Data Received From Active Radiator Air Flow Control Module A

common_causes: Battery disconnected or low voltage event
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0600.description: A control module reports that its non-volatile memory has been reset (lost adaptions, lost coding, lost trip counters). Often appears after battery disconnects, voltage drops below operating limit, or module reflashes.
U0600.title: Internal Control Module Memory Reset

common_causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
U0601.description: A control module has detected that its own internal software version is inconsistent — for example a partial flash that left the module with mismatched calibration and program code. The module may go offline or operate in a fallback mode.
U0601.title: Internal Control Module Software Incompatibility

U0602.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with smart particulate filter (DPF) differential pressure sensor B. The ECM cannot read soot loading via this channel and may switch to a model-based estimate.

U0603.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with smart fuel pressure sensor A (typically common-rail or low-pressure side). The ECM loses its actual rail-pressure feedback for closed-loop control.

U0604.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with smart fuel pressure sensor B (typically common-rail or low-pressure side). The ECM loses its actual rail-pressure feedback for closed-loop control.
U0604.title: Lost Communication With Fuel Pressure Sensor B

U0605.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with smart A/C refrigerant sensor A. Pressure or composition feedback for the refrigeration loop is unavailable; A/C may default to off.

U0606.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with smart throttle/pedal position sensor A. The ECM loses one of the redundant pedal channels and reverts to a fail-safe pedal map.

U0607.description: The vehicle bus reports loss of communication with smart throttle/pedal position sensor B. The ECM loses one of the redundant pedal channels and reverts to a fail-safe pedal map.
